Katalog Berita (Halaman 43/57)

#2827. Maresca singles out Leipzig duo after hard-fought Manchester City win

Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca singled out Brajan Gruda and Antonio Nusa following his side's hard-fought 3-2 win against RB Leipzig on Wednesday.

Leipzig fought back twice on the night, with the mentioned duo causing the visitors huge problems before Erling Haaland eventually sealed all three points.

Speaking to DAZN after the match, Maresca acknowledged that his side did struggle at the Red Bull Arena.

"Tough game. For some moments, I think we controlled quite well, but for some moments we struggled a little bit," the Italian admitted.

"But again, it's a Champions League game. Germany away, i's always difficult. So happy with the three points."

When quizzed on the tactical challenges presented by Leipzig, Maresca identified Gruda and Nusa as the two main threats.

"They are well organised. They were aggressive. On the ball, they are dangerous, especially with the two wingers, Gruda and Nusa. So we need to be careful also for the transition," he said, after taking on his former teammate Martín Demichelis - a manager who Maresca feels is doing a fine job in Saxony.

"A very good friend; we are very close. He's doing a fantastic job in the league. Also, in the Champions League, it's always difficult, and hopefully they can do better in the Champions League."

For now, attention turns to Augsburg on Saturday, before Leipzig have the chance to bounce back against RC Lens in Europe at the end of the month.

City, on the other hand, are looking to end their run of league defeats on Saturday as they travel to Nottingham Forest before the international break, while Fulham and Napoli visit the Etihad Stadium after the pause.

#2826. Sixers face Pistons with chance to avenge lone loss of the season

The Philadelphia 76ers begin a three-game road trip on Wednesday with a visit to the Detroit Pistons.

It'll be a battle of two teams enjoying red-hot starts to their 2026-27 seasons, with the Sixers coming into the matchup 7-1 and the Pistons 6-1. It's worth noting that the Sixers' lone loss so far this campaign came at the hands of the Pistons back on Oct. 25.

The Sixers' injury report is as clean as can be expected for this one, with only Dominick Barlow (back) and Ariel Hukporti (Achilles) on the list. For Detroit, they are still without Jalen Duren, who suffered a right hamstring strain in the second game of the season and has not returned since. They will also be without former 76er Isaiah Joe with a right hip contusion.

The loss of Duren as it happened seemed like it could be something that set the Pistons back a bit, but they've managed just fine so far. Cade Cunningham continues to be an effective offensive engine for Detroit, posting 23.7 points and 7.1 assists per game this season and is shooting 37.0% from deep on a 6.6 attempts-per-game clip.

In Duren's absence, former Sixer Paul Reed has stepped up in taking on the starting five position. Reed has started the last five contests for the Pistons and has averaged 13.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists. 1.6 steals and 1.4 blocks in that stint. Not only that, but Reed is shooting 65.0% from the floor (5.6-for-8.6) to start the year. The Sixers would love a backup center like that…

Looking at team numbers, the Pistons are currently the best in the association in defensive rating at 102.0, but the Sixers are right there with them in third at 105.1. Detroit is holding opposing offenses to shooting just 41.2% from the floor, the lowest mark in the league. The best way to break through that wall for Philly may be to do exactly what they did against the Bulls (who, yes, are a much worse team than the Pistons) in getting out ahead in transition as often and as quickly as possible. Giving them time to set up defensively will only make things harder for the Sixers, who are still admittedly finding their footing at times in the half court offense — something one would hope only gets better and better with more time together on the floor.

As I mentioned, the Sixers' only loss this season so far came at the hands of this Detroit squad when they faced off in South Philadelphia over a week ago, but the context surrounding that game is worth noting as well. The Sixers went into that matchup on the second leg of a back-to-back (versus the Pistons after a day off), with both Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe sidelined. Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying that because they've had some rest and are at full strength that it'll be some cakewalk for Philadelphia tonight… but I think it certainly won't hurt their cause.

Both teams come into Wednesday on a three-game winning streak, but only one can remain near-perfect on the season after tonight.

The Sixers and Pistons tip off at 7 p.m. ET.

When: Wednesday, November 4, 7 p.m. ETWhere: Little Caesars Arena, Detroit, MIWatch: ESPN, NBC Sports PhiladelphiaRadio: 97.5 The FanaticFollow: @LibertyBallers

#2825. Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 9

The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (at MIA) - 133.5 proj. total yards

Gibbs survived the Vikings matchup with a top-5 finish in Week 8. Things will get easier from there. A lot easier. Across the season, Gibbs is averaging 25.5 half PPR points (RB1) on 23.7 expected points (RB1). He's leading in carries per game and second in receptions per game. What a season.

Miami ranks ninth-worst in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields (22.5 per game) and sits second in receiving points allowed to RBs. Detroit carries an implied team total of 28.75 points (third) as 7-point road favorites. This is obviously a smash spot, duh.

2. Kenneth Walker III (vs. NYJ) - 113.5 proj. total yards

Walker has had slower games against the Seahawks and healthy Broncos defenses, both clearly top-5 units to me right now. It hasn't helped that LT Josh Simmons (back/other) and LG Kingsley Suamataia (benched) haven't been active, forcing the Chiefs to dial up a ton of their runs to the right side only. Still, Walker is the RB6 on RB3 usage this month and RB2 in both metrics across the entire season. The offense at least getting Rashee Rice back in the mix will help them move the ball more often.

The Jets placed star DT T'Vondre Sweat on IR and first-round rookie DE David Bailey has missed time recently, too. They bottled up Mike Washington Jr. and the Raiders' disaster-class OL last week, but they're a unit to attack right now. Kansas City carries an implied total of 28 points (fourth) as 9.5-point home favorites.

3. Christian McCaffrey (vs. LV) - 96.5 proj. total yards

McCaffrey is the RB6 in half PPR points per game on RB6 usage across his last four games. They needed more receiving work from CMC during this stretch with Deebo Samuel Sr. and Mike Evans missing time, and we'll see if they return off the bye. He's better without them but has been a mid-range RB1 with the WRs healthy.

The Raiders rank fifth in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields (23.4 per game) and sit third in rushing points allowed to RBs, recently surrendering an RB6 finish to Braelon Allen. San Francisco enters with a slate-high 30.5-point implied team total (first) as 9.5-point home favorites. It's a great spot.

4. Bijan Robinson (vs. CIN) - 122.5 proj. total yards

Robinson is the RB30 on RB23 usage this month. I can promise that'll be the worst stretch of his season.

The primary driver of the falloff is the on/off splits with Michael Penix Jr. as a receiver. His targets with Penix this year are 3.2 per game. His career average for context is 5.1. Part of this is Penix's inability to move, which is required to buy time in the screen game or to work to the checkdown. The ball is flying out of his hand early in the snap, and those are less likely to go to RBs. Hopefully they carve out more looks moving forward. It'd be enough of a difference to view him in the mid-range RB1 tier, instead of the elite RB1 tier.

The Bengals are much improved against the run with superstar DT Dexter Lawrence shutting down everything up the middle, but the rest of the defense is looking suspect, especially if CB1 DJ Turner (ankle) can't go. The LB and S groups are missing huge tackles weekly, and Robinson is a great candidate to rip wide zone explosives away from Lawrence in the A gap. This is what Tony Pollard did last week when he was the RB3 overall. The Falcons carry a 24.25-point implied team total (12th) as 3-point home underdogs.

5. Javonte Williams (at IND) - 83.5 proj. total yards

Williams' lack of explosives is starting to cause the Cowboys' games, like last week in the second half when they leaned on the run game and it went nowhere. For fantasy purposes, it largely hasn't mattered because of his red-zone role in this top-10 offense. He's the RB12 on RB4 usage this season, despite being the RB11 in carries and RB23 in receptions.

His fantasy RB1 value is completely tied to scoring touchdowns. Since joining the Cowboys, he's averaged 16.5 points when they've scored 30+ points versus 15.1 in the 20s and 9.4 in the teens.

The good news is the Cowboys project for 28.75 points (second) against a Colts defense that looks lifeless without DT DeForest Buckner. Bhayshul Tuten just finished as the RB2 without playing the fourth quarter, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. was trucking defenders himself. Indianapolis has allowed the sixth-most rushing yards per game this season, and that will probably only get worse.

6. James Cook III (at MIN) - 97.5 proj. total yards

Truly nothing has changed. Cook is the RB4 on RB9 usage this season, averaging 101 rushing YPG (third) on RB41 receptions per game. The Bills offense looked particularly great last week with DJ Moore stretching the field and Dalton Kincaid ripping explosives in multiple TE sets.

The challenge here is the Vikings defense. They just held the Lions to 19 points on the road and are clearly one of the only truly elite defenses. Detroit leaned on the ground game a bit more than usual against them, a trend that's appeared throughout the season against Minnesota. It's allowed the No. 16 rushing YPG versus the No. 31 passing YPG. Opposing offenses have a 45% neutral pass rate against them (second lowest). That said, Jahmyr Gibbs (RB5) and Jonathan Taylor (RB8) both held the line, while mediocre schemes/players have completely busted. Buffalo heads to Minnesota as 3.5-point road favorites with a 25-point implied team total (11th).

7. Bucky Irving (at CHI) - 83.5 proj. total yards

The Bucs are coming off the craziest two-game run script I can remember. Irving has been the RB4 and RB11, respectively in expected half PPR points in them, while Kenny Gainwell has popped off alongside him. Tampa Bay is content running the ball behind its fantastic OL, and while it won't be anywhere near this extreme, I don't see that game plan changing after Baker Mayfield struggled in a pass-first offense early on. Irving's vision and contact balance are a great fit to consistently hit these 20-yard runs. This month, Irving is the RB2 on RB3 usage. He handled the goal-line carry last week, while Sean Tucker looked on from the sideline.

The Bears defense has been stingy against opposing backfields, ranking 29th in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 16.7 per game. Then they added the best DT in Jeffery Simmons. This will be a tough test for an on-fire Bucs run game. The Bears held Bijan Robinson to an RB31 finish in Week 6 and bottled up both Seahawks RBs last week. Tampa Bay heads on the road as 5.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 21 points (22nd).

8. Chuba Hubbard (vs. DEN) - 90.5 proj. total yards

Hubbard has been a high-volume anchor, sitting as the RB9 in per-game half PPR points on RB6 usage across his last four contests despite some difficult matchups. He's handled 19.3 carries per game (RB7) over that window, crossing the 20-carry threshold in three of those four outings. In Week 8 against Green Bay, Hubbard set season highs with eight targets and seven receptions, turning that receiving work into 21.4 half PPR points on 24.1 expected points. Jonathon Brooks is starting to practice, but they'll ramp him up slowly and he's unlikely to factor in too much when he is cleared.

The Broncos defense ranks 11th in half PPR points allowed to RBs at 21.9 per game on the season, but their starting lineup is finally back to normal. Opponents have had success through the air against Denver, where the defense allows 8.5 half PPR points per game to receiving RBs (fourth-most in the NFL), highlighted by Emmett Johnson's RB5 finish in Week 8. Carolina's offense also brings distinctive passing tendencies, holding a 62% neutral pass rate that ranks third-highest in the league. The Panthers enter the matchup as 3-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 20.25 points (25th).

9. Josh Jacobs (at NE) - 69.5 proj. total yards

Jacobs was the RB1 overall in usage last week after being the RB5 in expected half PPR points in his debut. He's averaging 18.9 half PPR points on 23.4 expected, essentially trading a couple of runs for a couple of targets in this more pass-heavy Packers offense. That's a great trade-off in fantasy. For context, the Packers had a 46% neutral pass rate in 2024-25 versus a 56% rate this year.

On tape, Jacobs is not in his prime, nor is the Packers offensive line, so he'll definitely be an inefficient player. Green Bay can't trust MarShawn Lloyd in protection or to hit the right hole, so they'll live with whatever Jacobs can produce.

The Patriots rank 26th in half PPR points allowed to opposing running backs, giving up just 17.0 points per game to the position. This was true the year prior, so it's a matchup worth knocking expectations. Recent bell cows D'Andre Swift (RB13) and Braelon Allen (RB19) were just fine. Green Bay heads on the road as 3-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 22.25 points (17th).

The splits with Kyle Monangai are staggering. We'll see if he can get cleared this week. If not, Swift has enjoyed a month-long stretch of being the RB3 on RB2 usage overall.

Tampa Bay has once again been stout against backfields this season, ranking 31st in half PPR points allowed to RBs (14.5 per game). The Buccaneers have been especially tough on the ground, sitting 31st in rushing points allowed per game to the position. Just ask Bijan Robinson (RB28), Jaylen Warren (RB23) and Javonte Williams (RB19) this month. Chicago enters as 5.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 26.5 points (seventh).

Taylor had his worst game since Week 8 of 2024. That did come against the best fantasy RB defense (Jaguars), but it did also come without LG Quenton Nelson during the middle of Taylor's own trade talks. The Colts been mixing in Seth McGowen earlier in games more than they did before, and their defense is getting blown out, which means Taylor can get scripted out of games. It's nowhere near the same situation as before, dropping him to boom-bust RB2 levels. I anticipate him being far more matchup-elastic given his poor surroundings.

Luckily, the Cowboys are a great spot. They've allowed the third-most fantasy points to RBs on the most rushing yards per game (152.8). It was Tyler Allgeier's turn last week (RB1 overall), but Saquon Barkley looked good on his limited touches the week prior and Bucky Irving dropped 175 yards in Week 5, too. It's bad versus bad on this side of the ball. The Colts have a 22.75-point team total here. It's a much better spot than last week, pending reports that Taylor's role could be changed the week before the trade deadline.

12. Kyren Williams (at WAS) - 84.5 proj. total yards

Williams' role is nearly the same, but the Rams offense hasn't been quite as explosive recently, so his output has slightly turned down. This month, he's the RB17 on RB16 usage, averaging 14.5 carries and 3.0 receptions. He was catching more passes early on, and it's possible the increased usage of 13-personnel is working against his passing role. Blake Corum continues to play every other drive; Corum is an NFL starter on tape to me.

Washington sits 27th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 17.0 per game on the season, but DT Daron Payne just went to IR. The top-end RBs have played well, including Christian McCaffrey (RB2) and Jonathan Taylor (RB9). Even Saquon Barkley (RB21 in a part-time role) looked good last week. The Rams travel as 5.5-point road favorites, carrying an implied team total of 26.5 points (eighth).

Tuten is a game-time decision with an ankle/foot injury. He hasn't practiced yet but his last play in Week 8 was a touchdown that didn't look painful. This is a good reminder that Chris Rodriguez Jr. is one of the top insurance options in fantasy.

Tuten sits as the RB10 in per-game half PPR scoring on RB18 usage over his last four contests. He has generated efficient production on the ground and through the air, averaging 72 rushing yards (RB13) and 36.3 receiving yards per game (RB7) across that window. Coming off a bye in Week 8, Tuten set season highs with 28.9 half PPR points (RB2) and 104 rushing yards against Indianapolis. The potential for a low-end RB1 finish following that Week 7 bye is pretty clear.

The Ravens present a difficult matchup, ranking 23rd in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 17.3 per game. Baltimore is particularly stout against pass-catching backs, ranking 29th by allowing just 3.7 half PPR receiving points per game. That matches its recent stretch, having limited Chase Brown (RB36) and Bijan Robinson (RB18) to modest days in Weeks 7 and 5, respectively. The Jaguars enter Thursday night as 8.5-point road favorites with an implied total of 25.5 points (ninth).

14. Rhamondre Stevenson (vs. GB) - 86.5 proj. total yards

TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was ruled out early last week and missed Wednesday's practice once again. There are notable splits for Stevenson whether he plays or not. In seven games dating back to last year where Hendo missed or had fewer than five carries, Stevenson is the RB13 on RB16 usage. He drops to RB25 on RB39 usage in the other 19 games. This year, Stevenson is the RB20 on RB28 usage while he's been in and out of the mix. It helps if A.J. Brown and Hunter Henry join Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins on the sideline, too.

Green Bay represents a favorable rushing matchup, ranking seventh in half PPR points allowed to RBs at 23.1 per game. The Packers sit sixth in points allowed to RB rushing at 16.6 per game, having yielded top-24 fantasy finishes to Chuba Hubbard (RB7), Jahmyr Gibbs (RB18), Javonte Williams (RB17) and D'Andre Swift (RB12) in four consecutive weeks. New England hosts the Packers as 3-point home favorites with an implied team total of 25.25 points (10th).

15. Jonah Coleman (at CAR) - 86.5 proj. total yards

With RJ Harvey (knee) on IR, the backfield was down to two. JK Dobbins started, but just like last week, it was Coleman who ended it. Dobbins was held to just one (one) snap in the second half of Week 8, while Coleman was left wide open for a 51-yard reception and ultimately cut back on a separate carry for a score. He finished as the RB11 on RB6 usage, tallying 11 carries and four receptions. He handled goal-line carries on separate drives, too.

Coleman has a little windup step when buying time as a runner, and he can find some cutback lanes that others won't see. He is a low-built power runner who will try to lower his shoulder for an extra yard. At the same time, he's probably the slowest fantasy starter and did bounce some runs to play into his weakness. He looks like a Day 3 talent who is climbing the depth chart by having fresh legs with some established trust. It's unlikely that Dobbins ever threatens on passing downs, so Coleman is at least the passing-down back with an emerging rushing role. We'll see if the Broncos actually trade for Jonathan Taylor later on. For now, Coleman is an RB2/3.

The upcoming matchup brings a Carolina defense allowing 26.1 half PPR points per game to running backs (second most). The Panthers have been particularly vulnerable on the ground, ranking second in rushing fantasy points allowed to opposing backfields. Recent opposing rushers have capitalized, including Bucky Irving (RB2) and Josh Jacobs (RB10). Denver heads in as 3-point road favorites with an implied team total of 23.25 points (13th).

16. Chase Brown (at ATL) - 73.5 proj. total yards

Brown was the RB20 on RB14 usage last week despite finishing with eight receptions. The good news is Brown still has 8-catch grabs in his pocket and those eventually will lead to more explosives and touchdowns. The problem was he played 2 of 8 snaps inside the 10-yard line, including 1 of 4 inside the 5-yard line. That's where Samaje Perine is mixing in more than normal. Across the month, Brown is the dang RB39 on RB11 usage. He'll settle in as a fantasy RB2 with upside, but the pass game is too good and Brown is too mid to believe in a full top-10 RB1 rebound here.

The matchup with the Falcons is a solid one. They've allowed the sixth-most points to fantasy RBs and were just embarrassed by Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell last week. Atlanta has allowed a top-10 fantasy RB in 4 straight outings, and EDGE Samson Ebukam just went to IR. They've missed a LB, too. The Bengals project for 27.75 points (fifth).

17. Ollie Gordon II (vs. DET) - 84.5 proj. total yards

Gordon has taken on significant rushing volume, ranking as the RB16 in half PPR points per game on RB12 usage across his last four outings. Over that stretch, he is averaging 17.8 carries (10th) and 90 rushing yards (eighth), while logging nine carries inside the 5-yard line. His passing-game involvement remains minimal, however, so the risk of being scripted out of the game plan is concerning against great opponents.

The matchup is tough against a Lions defense allowing just 16.2 half PPR points per game to RBs (30th most). Detroit ranks 25th in rushing points allowed and 24th in receiving points allowed to opposing backfields. Miami operates with a run-heavy approach, ranking 30th in neutral pass rate at 44%, while Detroit opponents pass at an extreme 59% clip (third highest). The Dolphins enter as 7-point home underdogs with an implied total of 21.75 points (18th).

Lions LB Jack Campbell will not be out there. It was relieving to hear that he has movement in his lower extremities.

18. Woody Marks (at LAC) - 78.5 proj. total yards

It sounds like David Montgomery is going to miss another one. In three games without him, Marks is the RB29 on RB17 usage, 16.3 carries and 2.7 targets per game. Marks is a replacement-level back who can play in all phases, but expecting efficient outings behind this OL is asking too much. He's finished below his expected half PPR point totals in 5 of 7 games.

The good news is the Chargers' run defense isn't one to fear. They rank 10th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 22.2 per game. Los Angeles has been particularly vulnerable against ground games, ranking fourth in rushing points allowed per game to running backs (17.3) while ranking 27th against RB receiving. It's allowed a top-16 finish in 4 straight games, including Blake Corum (RB15), Kenneth Walker (RB1), J.K. Dobbins (RB16), and Emanuel Wilson (RB6). Houston enters the contest as 4.5-point road favorites with a 22.5-point implied team total (16th).

19. Saquon Barkley (vs. NYG) - 77.5 proj. total yards

Barkley scored in the red zone on a Wildcat run, showcasing enough speed to get to the pylon. He generally looked just fine on tape, but the Eagles had to bring down his workload again. He's been the RB32 and RB22 in usage over the past two games, and in Week 8, he played just one snap on late downs and 44% of snaps on early downs. It'll be hard to reach top-15 status until he's unbothered by his back and hamstring.

A date with the Giants is neutral, revenge game aside. They're mediocre against the run in general, but both teams can play a run-heavy, slow-paced style that limits fantasy points in general. The Eagles only have an 18.0-point team total; we'll see if anything changes with QB Joe Milton starting over Tanner McKee.

20. Cam Skattebo (at PHI) - 74.5 proj. total yards

Skattebo (hamstring) was working on the side on Wednesday. Make sure Devin Singletary is rostered in your leagues.

The easiest way to parse through Skattebo's rocky 2026 season is to throw out his benching game and include the rest. He's averaged 11.2 half PPR points on 11.4 expected points in the six non-benching games. In Week 7 without Najee Harris, Skattebo was the RB7 (18.6) on RB30 usage (9.1 expected) while easily leading the backfield with 18 touches. Tyrone Tracy Jr. (hamstring) also left that game, potentially leaving Skattebo with Devin Singletary for the short term. He's by far their most powerful rusher, while Tracy and Singletary are change-of-pace players. This is a downhill team that will want to hide J.J. McCarthy as much as possible, so Skattebo is a candidate for 15-25 touches until proven otherwise.

21. Derrick Henry (vs. JAX) - 80.5 proj. total yards

Henry has played seven games without Lamar Jackson over the last three years, and he's averaging 16.8 half PPR points on 17.5 expected points and 22 carries per game. That's the absolute upside case, but the reality is his new baseline is far lower with Tyler Huntley also out and with OC Declan Doyle finding more ways to move the ball than running behind an aging Henry. The last month of the year are a great example of that, when he's been the RB28 on RB17 usage and 17.3 carries per game. That's a better baseline with "Joe Fagnano" under center on Thursday Night Football.

Jacksonville has been the most difficult fantasy RB matchup this year, allowing just 14.2 half PPR points per game to the position on the fewest rushing YPG (77.4). Opposing offenses have the lowest neutral run rate against them, too. It'll be a little easier without DT DaVon Hamilton, but this remains a matchup to avoid. The Ravens only have a 14.75-point team total as 10-point dogs. Henry can get game-scripted out of outings, just as Jonathan Taylor (RB37 on RB20) usage was last week.

22. Blake Corum (at WAS) - 59.5 proj. total yards

Judkins' role is changing for the worse with Dylan Sampson back in the mix. His expected half PPR points have dropped from 13.8 to 11.4 since his return and all of that has come from the receiving game, where his targets' split is 4.0 to 1.5. If the Browns start trailing, Judkins is now at risk of a total dud. He's been the RB22 and RB26 in usage over the last two outings and has been fairly inefficient throughout the year, making him a FLEX rather than a fantasy RB2.

The Saints represent a prime rushing matchup, ranking first in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 27.9 per game. New Orleans has been especially vulnerable on the ground, allowing a league-high 21.2 points per game to RB rushing (first of 32). Over their last four games, the Saints have yielded spike performances to Bijan Robinson (RB5), Brian Robinson (RB8), Aaron Jones (RB7) and Tyrone Tracy (RB8). Cleveland travels as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 20.5 points (24th).

We'll learn more later this week, but Hall is unlikely to return to his RB12, RB13 and RB33 finishes to start the year with Braelon Allen playing so well in his absence. That's particularly true with the Chiefs on deck. They've allowed the 25th-most rushing yards per game (96.3).

25. Rachaad White (vs. LAR) - 62.5 proj. total yards

Jeremy McNichols (foot) is going to miss months, leaving White and Austin Ekeler at the top of the pecking order with Devin Neal and Craig Reynolds available from the practice squad. White and Ekeler are battling it out in all phases, with White starting last week and finishing off the win with an explosive and goal-line TD late in the fourth quarter. White was the RB17 on RB17 usage last week and was the RB11 on RB22 usage before that. His fantasy low-end RB2 case is pretty straightforward.

The Rams rank 27th in half PPR points allowed per game to opposing backfields (17.0). Their DL is strong enough to overcome a scheme that is daring teams to run. Offenses facing Los Angeles have posted a 47% neutral pass rate, which is the third-lowest rate in the league. Because the Rams are light in the box and teams are often trailing, they have allowed the seventh-most receiving points to RBs, which plays into White's game. Ashton Jeanty was a PPR scam in Week 7 (RB10), and Bam Knight (RB20) and James Cook III (RB4) got home in the weeks before that. Washington is listed as a 5.5-point home underdog with an implied team total of 21.0 points (23rd).

26. Ashton Jeanty (at SF) - 64.5 proj. total yards

Jeanty is the first player to have the same or fewer carries in 8 straight games to open a season, per Doug Clawson on X. I don't think this was pre-game comments or ankle-related either. Coach Klint Kubiak has been scaling down his carries for a long time and communicated to Jeanty before this game of the role change.

Week 8 easily could be a one-game experiment to fix a completely broken run game, but it'd be a surprise if Jeanty went back to his early-season workhorse role. It's clear Kubiak, who pounded the table for Mike Washington Jr. and wasn't around for the Jeanty top-10 selection, views this duo as closer to even than Twitter does. Some of that is scheme-related, as Washington is a better athlete for the wide zone, while Jeanty's power-based skill set is struggling to find cutback lanes and hit the hole in time.

Jeanty's pass-game role is very safe, and I'm currently projecting a more even split on early-down runs, just how it has been from Week 3 on when he's been the RB18 on RB15 usage. The error bars here are obviously extremely wide, but if there's a game script that leans Jeanty, it's clearly while trailing. The Raiders are 10-point dogs to the 49ers.

27. Tyler Allgeier (at SEA) - 66.5 proj. total yards

With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) picking up his third separate high ankle sprain of the season, Allgeier has a chance to consolidate most of the Cardinals' touches. We'll see if Bam Knight (concussion) can get cleared in time. Without him, Allgeier is looking like one of the biggest workhorses of the week. The Cardinals' RB room collectively has averaged 21.5 expected half PPR points per game this year, and if he inherits 80% of that, then he's a top-24 option.

That will be stress-tested against the Seahawks, however. Gardner Minshew will make his first start against a top-2 defense. They've only allowed 94.0 YPG on the ground this year, and they recently kept Kenneth Walker III to 57 and Christian McCaffrey to 83 total yards. D'Andre Swift's 3-score outing on Monday Night Football is absolutely the exception, and the Cardinals unit is nowhere near the Bears'. Arizona has a highly concerning 14.5-point team total.

28. Jadarian Price (vs. ARI) - 55.5 proj. total yards

The backfield is set. #2824. Heartbreaking defeat! Lizelle Lee's rare wicketkeeping error denies Hobart Hurricanes a Super Over against Melbourne Renegade - Watch

Melbourne Renegades pulled off a dramatic four-wicket victory over Hobart Hurricanes in the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) on Wednesday, with a rare wicketkeeping infringement on the final delivery denying the hosts a chance to force a Super Over. Just when the Hurricanes appeared to have rescued a thrilling contest, Lizelle Lee's positioning behind the stumps turned the game on its head, handing the Renegades a victory through a no-ball decision at Bellerive Oval.Chasing 155, the Renegades needed one run from the final delivery with scores level at 154. Deandra Dottin failed to connect with Nicola Carey's delivery, and Lee collected the ball behind the stumps. Both teams appeared to be preparing for a Super Over, but the third umpire intervened after television replays showed that Lee had collected the ball in front of the stumps.Under Law 27.3, a wicketkeeper must remain wholly behind the striker's wicket until the ball touches the batter or their bat, passes the wicket, or the batter attempts a run. Any breach of this provision results in a no-ball being called. The decision awarded the Renegades the additional run they needed to seal a four-wicket win without a Super Over.

The dramatic finish followed another crucial twist in the final over. The Hurricanes were penalised for failing to complete their 20 overs within the stipulated time and were allowed only two fielders outside the 30-yard circle for the final three deliveries.After a dot ball, Dottin edged the penultimate delivery towards the deep third boundary. With the boundary rider unavailable because of the fielding restriction, the ball raced away for four, bringing the scores level at 154.Dottin then missed the final delivery, and Lee's infringement completed a remarkable turnaround for the visitors. The Hurricanes were left stunned as the Renegades celebrated their first victory of the WBBL|12 campaign.

Earlier, Hobart Hurricanes posted 154/7 in their 20 overs, with captain Nicola Carey leading the charge in her 150th WBBL appearance. Carey struck 62 off 43 deliveries, providing stability to an innings that saw the Hurricanes lose wickets at regular intervals.West Indian all-rounder Chinelle Henry added a quickfire 36 off just 18 balls to give the hosts a late boost. However, Henry later hobbled off after bowling just one over, which cost 14 runs, with a suspected hip injury.Renegades captain Sophie Molineux led the bowling attack with figures of 4/22, taking her career WBBL tally to 101 wickets. She became only the second player in the franchise's history to reach the 100-wicket milestone, after Molly Strano.

In reply, Hayley Matthews kept the Renegades on course with an impressive 59 off 44 deliveries, while Courtney Webb contributed 29 off 25 balls. The pair helped the visitors build a strong platform before the Hurricanes fought back.The Renegades suffered a dramatic collapse, losing five wickets for 37 runs after reaching 101, bringing the contest back into balance. Matthews was dismissed by Heather Graham, while Molly Strano produced a superb catch-and-bowl effort to remove Molineux.With 33 runs required from the final four overs, the Renegades used the Power Surge to keep the chase alive. Despite the late setbacks, they eventually crossed the line in one of the most unusual finishes of the tournament.The victory gave the Renegades their first win of the WBBL season 12, while the Hurricanes remained without a win after three matches and at the bottom of the standings.

#2816. JJ Redick challenged the Lakers defensively vs. Heat, felt team’s response was ‘awesome’

Although the Miami Heat are off to a rocky, 2-5 start, they sit a respectable 13th in offensive rating and operate at a breakneck pace. It's a style that could catch any team off-guard — and it often has over the past year or so — especially one playing the second leg of a back-to-back as the Los Angeles Lakers were Monday night. This season, Miami touts the NBA's fastest time to shoot at 10.4 seconds per possession, according to inpredictable, and is fourth in transition frequency (18.4%), per Cleaning the Glass.

In the first half of Monday's duel, the Lakers struggled to corral Miami's uptempo attack. They surrendered 72 points before the break and led by just seven. After intermission, they held the Heat to 45 points and pulled away for a comfortable, 136-118 victory.

"We really challenged the guys at halftime. The biggest thing for us, the first thing on the scouting report was get back and get set," head coach JJ Redick told reporters after the win. "We had multiple clips and multiple guys, after makes, running towards our hoop instead of getting back. This was not a pick up, full-court game. They want to make it a track meet. They want to play high volume early offense."

According to NBA.com, the Lakers posted a 95.7 defensive rating in the second half. Redick attributes much of that success to slowing Miami's early attacks and containing its half-court offense, the former of which featured starkly different performances between halves.

"We gave up 40 points in the first half in the first eight seconds [of a Heat possession]. We gave up, I think, 16 in the second half in the first eight seconds and they were 0.71 [points per possession] in the half court, which is [the 98th percentile], is as good as you can kind of hope for," Redick said. "I thought the way they responded in the second half, or at halftime and then in the second half defensively, was awesome."

Despite being 6-2 with the league's second-ranked offense and fourth-best net rating, the Lakers are just 18th in defensive rating thus far. Moving forward, they'll hope they can parlay Monday's impressive second half into a prolonged stretch of feisty defense to complement their abundantly potent offense.

#2812. 49ers will have to make a decision on Brandon Aiyuk, sooner or later

With 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk finally doing what he should have done months ago, the ball will return to the team’s court.

The process for being reinstated from the reserve/left squad list is believed to be administrative. (Then again, the process of applying for the supplemental draft was believed to be administrative, too; Brendan Sorsby learned otherwise.) Once the league reinstates Aiyuk, the 49ers will have to put him on the roster, trade him, or cut him.

The 49ers could emerge from the situation with a roster exemption, which would buy them some time — and which would force Aiyuk to follow through on the obligation to show up, take a physical, and see what happens next.

The 49ers would then have options. Aiyuk would have to take a physical. If he fails, the 49ers could deem it to be a non-football injury. That would allow them to park him on the reserve/NFI list and not pay him.

They could try to trade him before Tuesday’s deadline, but no trade would happen without Aiyuk restructuring his contract to the league minimum, or something close to it. A trade seems highly unlikely, given that his 2026 base salary is $26.150 million.

The simplest outcome would be for the 49ers to cut him, and to let him sign wherever he wants. (If they cut him after the trade deadline, he’d have to pass through waivers. No one would claim his contract as it’s currently written.)

The biggest question is whether the 49ers will simply wash their hands of Aiyuk or play hardball with him. Hard feelings linger, given the way the relationship disintegrated.

It all comes down to whether the 49ers want to spend the time and effort necessary to make it as difficult as they can for him to get what he clearly wants: The ability to sign with any team he chooses.

He has said he wants to play for the Commanders. It’s still unknown whether the Commanders would want him. It’s also unknown whether anyone else would want him.

None of that matters until the 49ers release him. It’s possible, in theory, that they try to find a way to keep him on ice without paying him.

#2811. The rise of Cooper Flagg: How the Mavericks' teenage star is leading the franchise forward

DALLAS — Not long after an emotional NBA Cup win over the Houston Rockets on Friday, Cooper Flagg was asked about the joys of the Dallas' Mavericks' new two-star dynamic. Flagg and Kyrie Irving had combined for 68 points, 15 assists and 13 rebounds in the contest, the Mavs' third win in a row. But the 19-year-old didn't want to focus on himself or take away from his team's achievement against a legitimate contender.

Flagg redirected the question to preach about players excelling in their various roles regardless of perceived status.

Such a remark can be lost in a postgame interview, especially one where the subject tends to keep things brief and direct. But in that moment, Flagg was displaying a level of leadership that is typically unbeknownst to teenagers, much less budding superstars being handed the keys to a franchise.

(Mallory Bielecki/Yahoo Sports Illustration)

In three months, it will mark two years since the stunning Dallas trade that sent Luka Dončić to Los Angeles in exchange for Anthony Davis. The massive void left by Dončić and the emotional toll from such a jarring move created a butterfly effect for the city and organization, ultimately leading to the drafting of Flagg, but also the firing of head coach Jason Kidd and general manager Nico Harrison, and the hiring of Dusty May and Masai Ujiri this offseason.

But beauty can emerge from despair. So when May and Ujiri embraced in the tunnel after the final buzzer against Houston, hope re-emerged. And although the transition between eras has certainly come with its fair share of detours, Flagg's growing leadership in Year 2 — and, more importantly, his veteran teammates empowering him — has provided a North Star to follow.

"He's taken a step into a leadership role," teammate Daniel Gafford said. "There's different ways you can lead in certain areas. With Coop, he just finds ways to have fun throughout the craziest times. Kyrie [Irving] is one of the biggest leaders in the locker room and he leads by his voice and example. Coop is following suit and taking notes and doing it himself."

"It's huge," Flagg added. "Just getting the respect of my peers and teammates last year was big for me. They're trusting me, I'm trusting myself. It's a good recipe."

Flagg's mental growth has been concurrent with his on-court development. In the shot clock era, there are only 20 players who have averaged 25 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists, a steal and a block per game. At 19, Flagg is the youngest ever to reach those benchmarks.

Ironically, part of his success stems from the chaos he was born into. As a rookie under Kidd, Flagg was originally miscast as a point guard with questionable spacing at times, and at other junctures shared a backcourt with the likes of Brandon Williams, Ryan Nembhard and D'Angelo Russell — hardly a trio of names that screams development. Flagg also was a victim of Dallas' rotational roulette; only Cleveland and Washington had their most common lineups on the floor together less than Flagg's most consistent one (92 minutes, per NBA.com tracking data) last season.

A year later, Flagg has a clear-cut role in a cleaner half-court setup and has taken lessons from his playmaking past and refined them. His processor has sped up as the game has slowed down for him, better understanding how to attack opposing defenders, crack open schemes and create the best shot for himself and those around him.

As his usage rate has risen, so too has his assist rate, with Flagg now operating in the 98th and 97th percentiles, respectively, per Cleaning the Glass. An increase in possessions as a ball-handler has resulted in top-20 marks in secondary assists, potential assists and assist points created. It's no surprise the Mavericks are 17 points per 100 half-court possessions better with Flagg on the floor.

Flip to a Mavs game on League Pass on a Tuesday night and you'll see Irving receive an inbounds pass, flip it to Flagg and jog to the opposing wing to let him go to work.

"Just comfortable," Flagg said on how he feels with the ball in the half-court. "I'm comfortable getting to my spots and with my teammates. Coach is putting me in great spots."

Dallas was one of the worst spacing units last season, but Flagg now has Irving (a career 40% 3-point shooter) and Max Christie (38%) next to him (and the hope is P.J. Washington returns to his 2024 form, where he shot 38% from deep). May also wants to play with pace and incorporates a high volume of pick-and-rolls to get both Flagg and Irving on the ball. The pace, space and freedom allow Flagg's unorthodox style to take form — more isolations, more midrange attempts and a better overall shot selection. (His 3-point efficiency, hovering around 23%, remains a work in progress, but he's been able to establish elite go-to moves that negate the need to launch unnecessary 3s into the sun.)

Flagg's improved comfort within the offense speaks to his relationship with May; an open, honest one that incorporates feedback and fluidity.

"It's been great," Flagg said of his bond with May. "He watched a ton of film from last year and knows my game pretty well. So just whatever he's seeing where he wants to put me, it's been working really well."

Still, arguably none of this is made possible without Irving's presence, patience and poise. For starters, his gravity alone makes Flagg's job easier on a nightly basis, drawing attention away from him and opening up more space to operate. But Irving's experience, having shared the spotlight with a plethora of big names during his tenure, makes the day-to-day easier as well. For what it's worth, the Mavericks have outscored opponents by 25 points in 98 minutes that Flagg and Irving have been on the floor together. It's been less of a turn-by-turn approach and more cooperative, with Irving wanting to push Flagg to be the best version of himself. As an elder statesman now, it's about giving back to the younger generation.

"It's been great," Irving said to Yahoo Sports. "In my first few years in the league, I had some good veterans — Anthony Parker, Antawn Jamison, Anderson Varejão — they were all good to me. But I was always trying to figure out what more I can do to bring to the team, and the best thing for me was being able to be honest about who I wanted to become in this league and how I was gonna accomplish it. It wasn't a solo job. I think he has a lot more patience than I did when I was his age. With the supporting cast around him, he can trust us with any information or questions he wants to ask."

It takes a village to raise young players. A head coach without NBA experience forced to lean on his roster, creativity and communication. A wily, sage veteran with championship experience that is hell-bent on pouring into the next phase of NBA basketball. A community that supports and sees the full potential of an ascending superstar.

There's still work to do. The Mavericks, despite their winning record, are just 18th in net rating. And it's not just their conference that remains a gauntlet; their own division — with the Rockets, Spurs and Grizzlies ahead of them — is as deep as ever. But with Flagg's continued trajectory, along with the other now-stable pieces in place, Dallas' future is much brighter than its recent past.

"There's always so much room for improvement," Flagg said. "I haven't shot the ball incredibly well behind the arc. But just continuing to play at my own pace, getting better and cleaning up the turnovers. There's always room for improvement."

Bayern face Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday before taking on Mainz in the Bundesliga on Saturday in their final two matches ahead of the international break.

#2807. Andy Reid: Harrison Butker will remain the Chiefs' kicker

Despite missing a 54-yard field goal late in Sunday’s eventual loss to the Broncos, Harrison Butker will remain the Chiefs’ kicker.

#2806. Commanders Trade Pitch Sends $16 Million WR to Rams

The Washington Commanders might have an unexpected asset in their wide receiver room.

ESPN's Aaron Schatz thinks the Commanders might be able to swing a trade with the Los Angeles Rams that would send veteran Dyami Brown to the West Coast in exchange for a Day 3 pick before the November 10 NFL trade deadline.

"Brown is on a one-year deal; he would give the Rams a veteran field stretcher who could play some snaps while Davante Adams (hamstring) is out," Schatz wrote on November 4. "And as an added bonus, he's lauded as a run blocker. (Rams head coach ) Sean McVay loves wide receivers who can run block."

The Commanders are 2-4-1 and host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday in Week 9.

By the end of training camp, Hogs Haven's Scott Bair put Brown at the top of his list of Commanders who should potentially be traded in the near future.

"Dyami Brown has had a strong camp, especially of late, yet sits squarely on the roster bubble in a deep receiver group," Bair wrote on August 27. "The Stefon Diggs signing changed this position group, bumping those seemingly competing for prominent roles deeper on the depth chart. Return ability is a factor here as well, which is why Jaylin Lane and (to a lesser extent) Luke McCaffrey seem safe. That puts Brown and Treylon Burks in a bout for the No. 6 receiver spot – keeping seven doesn't seem likely – and could make one of them a trade target. Brown could fetch a bit more considering his speed and consistent availability, and Burks is a big-play option who provides injury protection and a big-body in the pattern. Washington could trade Brown and be okay."

Brown, a former 3rd-round pick, has underperformed at every moment of his career except for 1.

Fortunately for Brown — and his bank account — it was the most important moment of his career.

Were it not for that bravura stretch of games for the Washington Commanders in the playoffs following the 2024 season, Brown surely wouldn't have landed a 1-year, $10 million contract with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2025 or made his way back to the Commanders in 2026 on a 1-year, $1.75 million contract.

What's been lost in all of this is that Brown might have the worst hands of any wide receiver in the NFL. In 2025, Brown was second in the NFL in drop rate at 13.5 percent, behind Atlanta Falcons wide receiver David Sills at 13.9 percent.

The Jaguars were in desperate need of help from Brown, who was a stunning disappointment in his 1 season there with 20 receptions for 220 yards and 1 touchdown in 14 games. He will have approximately $16.7 million in career earnings after the 2016 season.

The discourse around LeBron James' decision to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in favor of the Philadelphia 76ers is still raging, despite the decision being months old at this point.

James' agent Rich Paul and Max Kellerman discussed this during a recent episode of their "Game Over" podcast.

"When you're in years 22, 23, 24, and you still have something left in the tank, it is a beautiful situation where you can position yourself alongside other guys that can play roles at a high level that give you a real chance of winning. And you don't have to try to be someone that you're no longer capable of being today," Paul said.

Rich Paul speaking about LeBron James playing on the Philadelphia 76ers during the "Game Over" podcast. (X/@NBA_Courtside).

"What gave rise to that was a change of location. Lakers didn't have that. They didn't have that… That's one of the reasons he picked Philadelphia," Kellerman said, which Paul agreed with.

Paul did give the Lakers credit at another point in the podcast, saying that they made good moves in free agency to add pieces around Luka Dončić after LeBron's exit.

Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James wears a vote shirt before a game against the Chicago Bulls at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Nov. 2, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers talks with referee Nick Buchert (3) during the first quarter of an NBA game in Los Angeles, Nov. 2, 2026. Getty Images

#2801. Warriors reportedly not paying Kristaps Porziņģis as he contemplates NBA future

Kristaps Porziņģis is reportedly not being paid any of his $20 million salary by the Golden State Warriors since he is not playing, according to ESPN's Shams Charania and Anthony Slater.

Porziņģis, who is away from the team as he deals with recurring POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome) symptoms, remains in play as the Warriors seek to move the 31-year-old forward before the Feb. 11 NBA trade deadline while they continue not paying him.

There are reportedly no plans for the Warriors to void Porziņģis' contract and the player is not disputing the lack of payments. He signed a two-year, $40 million contract in the summer with only $3 million guaranteed in the second season of the deal.

According to Bobby Marks, the decision is costing Porziņģis $218,341 per game.

Porziņģis released a statement last month saying that he was working with doctors to find a way back to better health after Charania reported the veteran was contemplating his future.

According to Cleveland Clinic, "POTS is a condition that causes your heart to beat faster than normal when you go from sitting or lying down to standing up." Symptoms can vary widely from patient to patient, but Porziņģis' seem more respiratory and fatigue-related.

POTS significantly limited the 7-foot-2 Porziņģis during the 2024-25 Eastern Conference semifinals against the New York Knicks, when he was with the Boston Celtics.

Porziņģis averaged just 15.5 minutes in that six-game series, which ended Boston's NBA title defense, with Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla revealing after Game 5 that Porziņģis didn't play the second half because "he couldn't breathe."

Over his 10-year career, Porziņģis has played 533 games and has averaged 19.5 points, 7.6 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game.

Last season, he split time between the Atlanta Hawks and the Warriors, appearing in 32 games, the fewest he's played in a season in his career outside of the missed 2018-19 campaign.

#2799. Dan Campbell and Jeff Hafley agree: Dolphins now are like Lions at start of their rebuild

In Dan Campbell’s first season as the Lions’ head coach, he went 3-13-1. By Year 2 the Lions had improved to 9-8, and in Year 3 they were in the NFC Championship Game. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley wants to build his team the way Campbell built the Lions, and Campbell thinks Hafley is doing it the right way.

With the Dolphins set to face the Lions on Sunday, both Hafley and Campbell said today that they see similarities between where the Dolphins are now and where the Lions were in Campbell’s first season: Building a winning culture, even if their record doesn’t show it yet.

“That’s how I want to play football. Let me retract that: That’s how we are playing football,” Hafley said of the way the Lions play. “I think if you watch us right now, every coach has said it, and everyone who watches us, whether it’s on TV or they turn on the tape, I get texts or phone calls, that’s what’s showing up on tape right now. And while it’s disappointing that we’re 1-6, the foundation of that with young guys, that’s really important to us. When you see the physicality and the toughness and how hard guys are playing, it means that they’re playing for each other and they’re bought in. We’ve brought the right guys here. That’s very, very important to me, and it will continue to be.”

Campbell said he thinks Hafley is building his team exactly the way a new coach should.

“Coach Hafley’s done a good job in his first year,” Campbell said. “A lot of similarities — it reminds me of what we were when we came in. They’re young, they’re hungry, they’re active, they run, they hit, they hustle, they finish, try to play disciplined ball. And they’re playing that way.”

#2798. Former Browns Safety Calls Mason McCormick a Dirty Player: ‘Proved His Point Right’

Former Cleveland Browns safety T.J. Ward called out Pittsburgh Steelers left guard Mason McCormick for slamming Jared Verse on his head during Sunday's game.

McCormick was called for a personal foul on Verse on an extra point after Rico Dowdle's touchdown run in the first quarter.

McCormick threw Verse to the ground after he leaped to block the extra point.

Verse said after the Browns' Week 4 win over the Steelers that Pittsburgh's offensive line "plays dirty." Ward thinks Verse is just calling it how it is.

"They proved his point right. That's a dirty-ass play," Ward said on the Speakeasy podcast. "You can't pick nobody up on field goal block and dump them on their head. You can't do that. That's illegal. Did he play well? No. Was his point proven? Yes. That's a dirty-ass play, whether it was warranted or not."

Mason McCormick called for a personal foul against Jared Verse on the extra point.Awfully soft. We've already heard way more than we needed to from this officiating crew.pic.twitter.com/PzcfE2p7ql https://t.co/Y1UliZGnM9

— Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) November 1, 2026

Verse made his thoughts clear about McCormick after the game.

"Like what I've said before about them, that's just the way that they are. Him specifically, that's the way he plays. That was just a lack of awareness on my part. I should've had a better grasp of the type of player I was going up against. That's on me," Verse said about leaping on the goal line.

Verse added: "To do something like that, I just can't have respect for that.

"I jumped in the air, tried to block the kick. He swept my legs in the air, ended up landing on my head. That's football. I'm very upset about it and if this wasn't football, I'd be acting a different way. He got a flag; we were able to walk away with a yellow penalty on them."

When asked if it was a dirty play, Verse said, "The refs called it how they called it. I'm not going to add any more fuel to the fire. But I thought it was a very uncalled for play."

#2796. Which NFL coaches are on the hot seat?

The NFL regular season is approaching its halfway point, and for some head coaches, the pressure to turn things around is becoming impossible to ignore. With playoff hopes fading for several teams, questions about leadership, accountability and the direction of struggling franchises are beginning to take center stage.

The NFL's coaching carousel is always one of the league's biggest storylines, but the decisions made over the next several weeks could determine which coaches survive and which organizations decide it's time for a change. Some coaches may still have enough time to salvage their seasons, while others are running out of opportunities to prove they're the right person for the job.

In this edition of "Safe or Fire," we'll evaluate coaches across the league whose seats are heating up, examining whether they deserve another opportunity or if their respective teams should begin looking elsewhere.

The Chargers are 0-7 and Harbaugh is 0-10 in his last 10 games. It's been tough to watch this year especially as Los Angeles had playoff expectations (and favorable preseason Super Bowl odds). Herbert looks lost for a coach known for being a quarterback whisperer.

Dallas has Texas sized expectations. With Brian Schottenheimer failing to address its defensive woes in two straight seasons, you wonder how patient Jerry Jones will be? The bad collapses in Week 3 and Week 8 are concerning along with a dud to a Bucs team without Baker Mayfield in Week 5.

#2794. Steve Kerr clowns Republicans after midterms for not getting the “Trump Dividend”

In the days leading up to the 2026 midterm elections across the nation, United States President Donald Trump ran an ad featuring Trump promising Americans a $5,000 check if Republicans keep control of Congress. The ad even found its way onto UFC Fight Night broadcast the Saturday before election day.

Knowing that Trump and the Republican party were polling horribly leading up to the election, in large part due to gas prices spiking since the United States launched strikes on Iran earlier this year, the "Trump dividend" of $5,000 was promised to every American if Republicans hold on to both the House and Senate. Although Congress would still have had to approve the checks before anyone saw any money, it was ultimately a moot point.

The Democrats dominated Tuesday's elections across the nation and gained control of both the House and the Senate. On Wednesday, Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr, a longtime Trump critic, even took a dig at the President and his dividend.

"What no questions on the election? I'm surprised," Kerr said during his media availability. "I'm just I'm disappointed because I was looking forward to that $5,000 check that we were all going to get. I thought for sure… I already spent it in fact… Now, I'm gonna have to figure something out."

In April, when it was uncertain whether Kerr would be returning as the coach of the Warriors, NBA reporter Marc J. Spears is speculated that some of the uncertainty might be tied to his willingness to speak on social justice issues.

"He speaks out on social justice issues, he speaks out on racism issues, he speaks out on gun violence, and I've heard a little bit that maybe he's being stifled a little bit in that regard," Spears said.

Ultimately, it proved to be a non-issue, as Kerr inked a lucrative extension to return, and it seems his outspokenness has come with him.

#2790. Peter Broome, former Acushnet exec and Canadian Golf Hall of Fame inductee, dies at 66

Longtime Acushnet executive Peter Broome died Wednesday after a battle with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). He was 66.

A devoted husband, father, grandfather and friend, Broome leaves behind a legacy defined by family, friendship, generosity and a lifelong love of the game of golf.

Born April 19, 1960, and raised in Montreal, Canada, Broome discovered golf at an early age and began building the foundation of his career as a junior member at Royal Montreal Golf Club and Mount Bruno Country Club.

Influenced by his father and former Royal Montreal head professional Bob Hogarth, Broome developed a deep appreciation for the role golf professionals play in the game. He followed a similar path, working as an assistant professional at several Montreal-area clubs while attending McGill University.

After earning his degree, Broome joined Acushnet in 1993, beginning a career that spanned nearly three decades with Titleist and FootJoy. He eventually relocated to the United States and worked from the company's Fairhaven, Massachusetts, headquarters. Broome retired in 2022 as senior vice president of Titleist brand management and industry relations. In that role, he oversaw partnerships and communications with key industry stakeholders, including the PGA of America, PGA Tour and golf's governing bodies, while also helping lead the company's operations in Canada and Latin America.

Diagnosed with ALS in August 2024, Broome confronted the disease with courage and dignity. While the illness gradually robbed him of many physical abilities, it never diminished his character, devotion to family or desire to help others. With the support of family and close friends, he helped establish the ALS Bridge Foundation, which works to accelerate research funding and expand access to ALS clinical trials. The foundation has already made a $1 million gift to ALS research at Massachusetts General Hospital and the Sean M. Healey & AMG Center for ALS.

Broome's contributions to the game were recognized by the PGA of America, PGA of Canada and Golf Canada. In 2025, he was named an honorary member of the PGA of America, becoming just the 13th person to receive the honor in the organization's history. The distinguished group of honorary members includes three U.S. presidents and entertainer Bob Hope. Mentoring PGA professionals throughout their careers was one of Broome's greatest passions, and many of those he mentored became lifelong friends.

Last month, Broome was inducted into the Canadian Golf Hall of Fame, an honor that meant the world to him. Although he spent much of his professional career in the U.S., he remained connected to his Canadian roots and to the game in his home country. Being recognized by the nation where his love for golf began ranks as one of the proudest moments of his life and career.

Despite his many accomplishments in golf, Broome's greatest source of pride and joy was his family. Alongside his beloved wife, Sandy, he built a life filled with love, laughter and cherished memories. He was a proud father to Valerie (Jon), Matthew (Caroline) and Brad (Juliette), and a loving grandfather to Peter, George and Jack.

Broome was admired not only for his leadership and contributions to the game, but also for his humility, integrity and genuine interest in others. He often said there were "no strangers in golf, only friends who haven't met yet," a philosophy he embodied throughout his life.

In lieu of flowers, the family asks that donations be made to the ALS Bridge Foundation in Broome's honor. They remain committed to carrying forward his mission of helping others affected by ALS and advancing the search for a cure.

This article originally appeared on Golfweek: Peter Broome, former Acushnet exec and Canadian Golf Hall of Fame inductee, dies at 66

#2788. Report: Warriors withholding payments to Kristaps Porzingis on $20M salary

The strange saga concerning the playing status of veteran forward Kristaps Porzingis continues, as the Golden State Warriors are reportedly not paying his $20 million salary for the 2025-26 season because he is not playing.

ESPN.com reported on Wednesday, Nov. 4 that the non-payment stems from Porzingis not rendering services to the team or fulfilling his contract. Porzingis has not played yet this season because of an undisclosed illness that the team has yet to clarify.

The Warriors can seek to trade Porzingis before the Feb. 11 trade deadline, as Porzingis has reportedly leaned toward retirement. The salary for the 31-year-old still counts against the salary cap and any tax apron that the Warriors could possibly pay.

Porzingis' two-year, $40 million deal expires at season's end, making him a prime trade candidate and allowing any acquiring team to shed salary on its own roster to create a roster spot, possibly for a playoff push. According to the report, Golden State is not currently entertaining voiding the remainder of his contract.

The Hawks traded Porzingis to Golden State for Jonathan Kuminga and Buddy Hield on Feb. 5, 2026. He played only 15 games with the Warriors and 32 games overall in the 2025-26 season.

Golden State saw enough potential to sign him to a two-year, $40 million extension in June, which came with a player option for the 2027-28 season. He was guaranteed $20 million for this season, but only $3 million was guaranteed in the last year of the deal.

Before training camp started, general manager Mike Dunleavy was called by Porzingis, who informed him he was stepping away from the team.

The team then said Porzingis would be around as he recovered from his illness, but he wouldn't play because of that medical condition.

In 12 NBA seasons, Porzingis has averaged 19.5 points and 7.6 rebounds for the New York Knicks, Dallas Mavericks, Washington Wizards and Boston Celtics, along with the Hawks and Warriors.

#2784. Iowa State basketball to retire Melvin Ejim's jersey during TCU game

AMES — In 2014, Melvin Ejim famously dropped a Big 12 single-game record 48 points on an ultra-efficient 20-of-24 shooting performance in a comfortable win over TCU.

Now, more than a decade later, Iowa State basketball will be celebrating his decorated career by retiring his jersey during halftime of the Feb. 27, 2027 home game against TCU.

The former Big 12 player of the year and All-American will get his No. 3 jersey retired and get a commemorative banner raised in the rafters of Hilton Coliseum. Iowa State first announced the decision to retire Ejim's number back in February, but it announced a set date and time for the official ceremony on Nov. 4.

He will become just the eighth Iowa State men's basketball player to have his jersey retired and the first since Barry Stevens received the honor in 2008. A 6-foot-7 forward from Toronto, Canada, Ejim enjoyed an illustrious career at Iowa State from 2010-14.

A four-year starter who appeared in 135 games, Ejim accumulated 1,643 points and 1,051 rebounds. There are only three Iowa State men's basketball players in the 1,000-point, 1,000-rebound club.

Ejim was initially recruited to Iowa State by then-assistant and Iowa State's current head coach T.J. Otzelberger to join Greg McDermott's team. McDermott ended up leaving Iowa State for Creighton, and Fred Hoiberg was subsequently hired in a move that would revitalize the program. Ejim was a cornerstone in the first few years of Hoiberg's tenure.

"I had a special four years in Ames," Ejim said in a statement. "We accomplished so much as a team. We worked hard to put Iowa State basketball on the map, and we are starting to see the fruits of our labor we put in to set the foundation for the program. I'm thrilled to see all the success they have had with T.J.

"I am so honored to have my jersey retired. As an athlete, you always want to be recognized for the work you have put in. I took pride in representing Iowa State in a first class manner, and to be recognized with the other incredible Cyclones in the rafters is amazing."

Ejim had one of the best senior seasons in program history. He averaged 17.8 points, 8.4 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 1.2 steals per game, while shooting 50.5% overall and 34.6% from deep. He was a catalyst in the Cyclones' 2013-14 season, which featured a then-record 14-game winning streak for the program's best start (a record broken by the 2025-26 team's 16-0 start).

After that record-setting start, the Cyclones went on to win a 2014 Big 12 Tournament title and reach the Sweet 16, things that hadn't been achieved since the 2000 Cyclones. Iowa State finished 28-8 that year, and Ejim was named Big 12 player of the year and an All-American.

Ejim was also named the All-Big 12 third team as a junior in 2012-13, after averaging 11.3 points and 9.3 rebounds per game.

After graduating from Iowa State, Ejim went overseas and continues to play professionally. He is currently a member of the Spanish Liga ACB team Força Lleida. He's been a part of eight title-winning teams throughout his time playing in Europe, including the time he led Reyer Venezia Mestreto to win the Italian League championship in 2017 while earning Finals MVP accolades.

Ejim has also played at an international level as a representative for Canada's national team. He's been an active member of Team Canada since 2013. He recently helped Canada take third in the 2023 FIBA World Cup, where they defeated Team USA in the bronze medal game. He was also selected as a member of Canada's 2024 Olympic basketball team.

In order to be considered for jersey retirement honor, an Iowa State student-athlete must have graduated, been inducted into the school's athletics hall of fame and earned a significant national or conference honor during their playing career.

A list of other Iowa State men's basketball players to get their jerseys retired prior to Melvin Ejim.

#2782. Pistons vs 76ers preview: East’s top two teams square off on National TV

If you are to believe preseason predictions, this game being a showdown between the East's top two teams could come as a bit of a surprise. Pistons fans knew this team would be good, but many talking heads predicted a falloff this season while everybody was on board with the 76ers being one of the best teams in the league.

It shouldn't come as a surprise that the team that was 1st in the East last season is once again competing for the top seed in the East, but talking heads have to make their money somehow. ESPN at least had the foresight to pickup this game and you get what should be a very fun early-season showdown between two teams that have only lost one game each.

The 76ers and Pistons have played once this season and the Pistons won, but it is tough to draw any conclusions since both teams were missing a couple of starters.

Where: Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, MIWhen: Wednesday, November 4 at 7 pm ESTWatch: ESPNOdds: Detroit (-2.5)

The Pistons will be without Jalen Duren and Isaiah Joe, who was already ruled out for this game last night. The Pistons were missing Jalen Duren in the last matchup between these teams and also Ausar Thompson, who they will have back. But, Isaiah Joe did suffer the hip injury that is still keeping him out during the 1st quarter of the last matchup, so the Pistons are trading one injured player for another.

With this being a National TV game and the 76ers getting a day of rest, I would suspect that everybody plays for them tonight. In the last matchup, the 76ers did not have Joel Embiid or VJ Edgecombe, which really put their lack of depth to the test.

Joel Embiid's size and ability on the glass could become a problem for the Pistons, who will continue to start the undersized Paul Reed and likely use John Collins to back him up. Without Jalen Duren, rebounding was already going to be a problem, but the Pistons have been able to overcome it during his absence.

In the last matchup, the Pistons were able to contain Tyrese Maxey through 3 quarters before he started hitting shots in the 4th. It was a bit of shocking development since the Pistons were without Ausar Thompson, but without some of the other stars for the 76ers, they could focus their defense more on stopping Maxey. The 76ers have a lot of star power, but their biggest offensive threat is arguably Maxey, who can hit shots from anywhere on the court and can use his quickness with the ball to get to where he wants. I would expect Ausar Thompson to draw the Tyrese Maxey matchup which will allow Cade Cunningham to guard Jaylen Brown since he has the size to keep up with him.

I am not really sure what the Pistons are going to do about the Joel Embiid matchup. Paul Reed is outsized by him and also can have some issues with fouling and Joel Embiid has made a living off of bating fouls throughout his career. Paul Reed is going to have to stay disciplined, as I don't think the Pistons can afford to have heavy minutes of John Collins at center or Tolu Smith. I have full confidence in the Pistons' ability to matchup with the rest of the 76ers starting lineup, but the most concern I have is this matchup and it very well could swing the game.

If there is one certainty for the Pistons, it is that Cade Cunningham is difficult to slow down, especially with how he is playing now. He is coming off a 33 points masterclass against the Charlotte Hornets on Monday in only 27 minutes where he absolutely took over the game and turned a single-digit lead into a 20-plus point blowout. Cade Cunningham always starts off the season slow, but he seems to be hitting his stride now. His 3-ball is consistently falling as he is shooting 37% from beyond the arc, which is a significant development for his offensive creation abilities and efficiency.

He is going to have to put together another masterclass if the Pistons want any hope to win this game. During Jalen Duren's absence, the Pistons have been able to win games through their high-level defense, but their offense has left a lot to be desired. With Isaiah Joe out and Duncan Robinson going through a bit of a cold stretch, the Pistons shooting fell off a bit and they went four games in a row scoring 110 points or less.

However, everything seemed to get back on track on Monday against the Hornets, so hopefully that continues.

One player the Pistons are hoping gets back on track is John Collins.
