#2780. No end in sight for Russell as he eyes famous All Blacks win

Such is the level of trepidation among Scotland fans as to what life will look like for their team in a post-Finn Russell world, the superstar fly-half has had to field questions for years now as to when he might think about hanging up the boots.

"I'm only 34 – you'd think I'm 44," Russell jokes on the BBC Scotland Rugby Podcast as he prepares for Scotland's Nations Championship showdown with the All Blacks at Murrayfield on Saturday.

"I'm feeling good just now. I think the year after the Lions takes a lot more out of the players than you think - mentally, physically, emotionally.

"It's a big, big high. It's a long season. I think to come back and play the next year as you had done the year before is quite tough.

"But this year I'm feeling much better. Fresher mentally, physically, feeling good going into this season and now I'm feeling good."

What can Scotland deliver in Autumn Tests?

Scotland have learned from painful loss to All Blacks - Cummings

The transplanted Scot doing famous father proud in New Zealand

The Lions tour of Australia last summer was Russell's third but the first in which he was the undisputed king of the 10 jersey. Leading the Lions to a series win down under was a fitting reward for one of the greatest players to ever pull on a Scottish jersey.

He laughs off questions about his career entering its final throes in typical Russell style, but there is a hint of frustration that the topic keeps coming up, probably because he feels there is so much left to do in the time he has left.

Title wins with Glasgow Warriors and Bath, a European final with Racing 92, three Lions tours and 95 caps for his country - Saturday will be his 100th international across Scotland and Lions Tests - is an impressive body of work, but finally winning something with the national team would surely top it all.

We know what Scotland can do at their best. They welcomed an England side on a 12-match winning run to Murrayfield in the last Six Nations and took them apart. They put 50-points on a French side that had looked on an unstoppable march to the Grand Slam.

They put seven tries on Argentina in Cordoba in the summer and, despite going down to South Africa the following week, the Scots ran in four tries and could have scored a few more as they gave the world champions an almighty scare in Pretoria.

At their best, they are a match for anyone, but their best often eludes them at the critical point in tournament rugby. How do Scotland make the step from a very good side to a title-winning one?

"It's the million-dollar question, isn't it?" Russell responds to a question he has been asked many times before.

"From the summer, we were really good against Argentina when we got into the 22 and we were really good at executing there. The percentage was really high.

"We actually had more chances, I think, or more entries against South Africa, but the conversion rate was a lot lower, probably half of what we had against Argentina. So, how to capitalise and convert when you get into the 22 is probably the main growth that we need to have."

Such was the nature of rugby's somewhat elitist approach to the international calendar, when the top five or six teams sides would be allowed to carve up the schedule to play among themselves in the big summer Test series, Saturday will be just the fourth time Russell will have a crack at the All Blacks in 12-and-a-half years of international rugby.

The new Nations Championship format has changed all that and Scotland will get more exposure to the southern hemisphere heavyweights going forward, but the Bath fly-half knows opportunities to be part of the team that smashes the 121-year-old barren run against New Zealand are running out.

He will get at least one more after this when the Scots travel to Dunedin for their final match before next year's Rugby World Cup, but here is an opportunity on Saturday to ensure they to go to New Zealand for Scotland's first away match against the All Blacks in 27 years with the hoodoo already consigned to history.

Russell's three matches against the All Blacks have all been close defeats, each agonising in their own unique way, but he believes the Scots are better for the experiences.

"It'll be really exciting to play them again at Murrayfield," he says. "It's always a great occasion.

"Obviously, there's a lot of footage from the All Blacks from the last few months that they've been playing against South Africa and Australia, so we'll look into that. The boys know [head coach, formerly of Glasgow] Dave Rennie and [former Edinburgh head coach, now All Blacks assistant] Mike Blair really well.

"Knowing them, they'll have something up their sleeve to attack us and to defend us, but just prepping as best we can to try and rip in and kick on from the summer that we had.

"We've definitely got the belief, but it's about going in and delivering the product on the field, I suppose, and turning them over.

"It's all very well having the belief, but we need to get the results from that."

#2777. Is the Lakers’ red-hot offense sustainable?

Back-to-back wins helped get the taste of a really frustrating loss out of the mouths of Lakers fans to start the week. The absurd play of Luka Dončić also helped us forget as well.

It's a fun time to be a Lakers fan, evidenced by Bill Simmons' anger about the Lakers. Anything to take his focus off Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown feuding, I guess.

We asked again for questions from you guys and, once again, you answered…or asked? Either way, there's plenty to talk about in this week's mailbag!

It might feel like the Lakers have an unsustainable offense, but I think some pretty encouraging numbers push back against that. So, let's dive into this because there is a lot to this.

First, let's look at the threes. Sure, many of Luka threes don't seem sustainable except that it's Luka taking those threes. But outside of that, the team is getting quality looks from beyond the arc.

The team is ninth in 3-point rate with 46% of their shots coming from beyond the arc. That's a drastic change from last year when they ranked 22nd at 39.4%.

More notably, the team was dead last in catch-and-shoot 3-pointers attempted and made last year and 24th in 3-pointers attempted overall. This season, it hasn't even been that drastic of an increase in volume, but it has improved. They're 16th in 3-pointers attempted, 25th in catch-and-shoot 3-pointers attempted and 19th in makes.

The biggest changes are that they rank second in 3-point percentage, first in catch-and-shoot 3-point percentage and eighth in wide-open 3-point percentage. And yet, they still rank just 15th in the percentage of their points coming from threes.

That's because they're still getting to the rim, too. Last season, they were basically, across the board, the best team at scoring once they got to the paint. It's the benefit of having LeBron James with Luka and Austin Reaves, two great finishers at the rim.

LeBron is, obviously, gone now. But for this specific stat, they replaced him with Walker Kessler, who has feasted at the rim as a roll man. Add in Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes, two players north of the 85th percentile in field goal percentage at the rim, and you see why the Lakers rank second in the league in field goal percentage at the rim and first in field goal percentage in the paint.

To perhaps lay this out a little differently, the Lakers opened the season with Walker Kessler flourishing in the pick and roll. Teams rightly decided that wasn't sustainable, so they started blitzing ballhandlers on ball screens and working to take away Kessler as a roll option.

The result is open 3-point shooters and the Lakers now have a team capable of punishing teams who leave them open. Certainly, they won't keep shooting this well, but this is also the type of offense head coach JJ Redick wants to run. He wants a modern offense that puts up lots of threes.

So, don't expect a change, but also don't be quite so worried about it being unsustainable.

LOS ANGELES, CA – NOVEMBER 1: Walker Kessler #14 of the Los Angeles Lakers blocks the shot of Collin Murray-Boyles #30 of the Toronto Raptors during the game between the Toronto Raptors and the Los Angeles Lakers on November 1, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images

Let's jump to the other side of the floor now and look at the defense.

The good news is that when you have an offense as good as the Lakers have had, you don't need to be great defensively to win. The bad news is, notably, bad defenses don't typically win at the highest levels.

As commenters pointed out, two areas are at least partly responsible for the poor defensive rating: turnovers and rebounding.

The Lakers currently rank 27th in the league in turnovers and 27th in opponent points off turnovers. Teams are taking advantage of the Lakers being sloppy.

They also rank 26th in offensive rebounds allowed. Not surprisingly, they rank 29th in opponent second chance points.

Defensively, they're great in lots of areas. They're fifth in steals, fourth in blocks and second in points off turnovers. They're mostly middle of the road or slightly below average in opponent field goal percentage (17th) and opponent 3-point percentage (23rd). And that's not based on shooting luck, as teams are hitting 38.8% of their open threes.

The more this group gains chemistry and familiarity, the better they'll look defensively as well. It's not as simple as fixing those two aspects and being a good defense, but those are the two glaring outliers right now.

The rotations have been pretty ironclad with Luka and Ausint since last year. Luka is going to play the entire first and third quarters and half of the second and fourth quarters to come in at around 36 minutes.

Austin will have his minutes broken up a bit more as he'll leave late in the first quarter, return to open the second, then take another break in the middle of the period before returning to close the frame. Then, he repeats that in the second half.

That has been the rotation for the last two seasons for those two. It ensures that one of them is always on the floor, which is the right approach, and keeps both of them around 36 minutes per game.

When you have two elite on-ball players, you want to give both chances to maximize that skill. Austin is a great off-ball player as well, but giving him his own lineups and time on the floor without Luka, and vice versa, means the Lakers will have a full 48 minutes of an All-Star-level player on the floor.

There will be concerns about both of them after the injuries last season. But the Lakers also need them on the floor as well and 36 minutes per game isn't an unreasonable expectation for a star.

The more likely route for them to get rest is nights off throughout the year. The team already rested Luka once and I imagine that'll happen with some regularity this season.

It's definitely fair to be put off by Quentin Grimes' slow start. Like many, I thought he would get a starting nod to open the season. But perhaps Redick and his staff saw what fans eventually saw when the season started, which was a fair amount of indecisiveness and uncertainty.

The good news is that we are only three weeks into the season and Grimes looked better in the most recent game. It's a matter of him eventually playing more on instinct rather than thinking through the game, which you can tell he's doing right now.

I actually think it'd be better for him, and the team long-term, to be in the starting lineup. It gives that group another creator and dynamic player who can drive or shoot. But it's hard to make the argument to start him based on how he's currently playing.

We're still quite a bit away from being too worried about Grimes. Instead, I'd rather celebrate finding two big wins in Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle so far.

First, I think in this specific play, their judgement was that Thybulle was in an illegal guarding position and committed a foul before any push off occurred. Because there's simply no way to argue there wasn't a push off.

Secondly, as will most things that are a point of emphasis to start the year, I don't suspect it will carry on into the season much. Stars aren't changing how they play to accommodate the rule change. It'll just continue business as usual.

#2776. NASCAR Cup Series Championship Preview: Larson Looks to Finish the Job at Homestead

The NASCAR Cup Series heads to Homestead-Miami Speedway this Sunday for the 2026 season finale, where one driver will be crowned champion. After a long season filled with dramatic finishes, surprise winners and intense playoff battles, everything comes down to one final race.

The NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race is scheduled for Sunday, November 8, at 3 p.m. ET on NBC. Drivers will compete for 267 laps around the 1.5 mile Homestead track, covering 400.5 miles.

Kyle Larson Enters With the Championship Advantage

Kyle Larson enters the championship race as the clear favorite after building a 67-point advantage over Christopher Bell. The Hendrick Motorsports driver has been one of the strongest competitors throughout the season and is looking to capture his third championship in six seasons.

Larson has also enjoyed success at Homestead, winning the most recent Cup race at the track in March 2025. His ability to run multiple grooves and maintain speed near the wall could make him especially dangerous on Sunday.

However, Larson cannot afford to make major mistakes. A difficult afternoon could give his championship competitors an opportunity to make things interesting.

Christopher Bell enters the finale 67 points behind Larson, while Denny Hamlin sits 70 points back. Both drivers will need an incredible performance and some help if they want to take the championship away from Larson.

Bell has already proven he can win at Homestead, capturing the victory in 2023. Hamlin also has plenty of experience at the track, with three career victories there.

Both drivers will need to focus on winning while hoping Larson experiences trouble.

Homestead Could Deliver an Exciting Finale

Homestead is known for its unique racing style, with multiple grooves allowing drivers to find different lines around the track. Tire management, handling and pit-road strategy will be extremely important over 267 laps.

Drivers such as Chase Briscoe, Tyler Reddick and William Byron could also be in position to challenge for the race victory.

Larson has the advantage, but nothing is guaranteed until the checkered flag waves. With Bell and Hamlin still mathematically alive, NASCAR fans have plenty of reasons to watch Sunday's finale.

One driver will leave Homestead as the 2026 Cup Series champion.

#2773. What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique

What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

They're a team of superstars that don't play superstar basketball.

That's the beauty of this 76ers team. They play a brand of unselfish team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars.

LeBron James is one of the two or three greatest players in NBA history, a four-time MVP, a four-time NBA champion, a 1st-ballot Hall of Famer.

Joel Embiid is a seven-time all-star, a former MVP, an Olympic gold medalist and a likely Hall of Famer.

Jaylen Brown is a five-time all-star, an NBA champion, a career 20 points-per-game scorer.

Tyrese Maxey is a two-time all-star, one of only two NBA guards averaging 27.0 points per game over the last four years.

Four certified megastars on one team. And somehow they've figured out how to leave their egos at the front door and play smart, tough, disciplined team basketball, the style of ball you just never see on these superstar-laden teams.

On offense, they patiently work the ball around, always looking for the open man or a positive matchup. You've got this bunch of big-name, high-priced All-Stars who are just as happy to pass the ball as shoot it. That never happens.

The 76ers are sixth in the NBA in assists, and they're one of only four teams with twice as many assists as turnovers. Smart, unselfish, patient, disciplined.

When an all-timer like LeBron averages 7.3 assists per game that speaks volumes. LeBron is fifth in the NBA in assists per game among forwards, which is wild. You can see the joy on his face when one of his passes leads to a basket. When one of the greatest players in history has that mentality, it rubs off on everyone around him.

Embiid hasn't really got going yet on offense and still takes too many 3's, but he's also embraced the team-first mentality, and his 4.8 assists per game are more than one full assist above his career average and 4th-most in the NBA among centers or forward-centers. And still one of the most dominating defensive players in the league.

Brown is averaging 27.0 points, which you expect, but he's also averaging 4.3 assists per game, significantly above his career average of 3.8 coming into the season. He's fit in so well so fast you forget its his first season here.

And what can you even say about Maxey? Just a beast. He's averaging nearly 30 points per game but never wastes a possession, always makes the right decision with the ball in his hands and is still finding time to average 4.3 assists per game.

With James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey, the 76ers are the only NBA team with four guys averaging at least 16 points and 4 assists per game. Only the Pacers, Magic and Raptors have three.

But where we're really seeing this group playing out of their minds is on the defensive end, where this bunch of all-stars, including two newcomers, has been astounding.

The 76ers have the 2nd-best defensive efficiency rating in the league, behind only the Pistons, who they play Wednesday night, and they're allowing the 2nd-fewest points in the league, also behind Detroit. Last year, they allowed 123 points per game through eight games. This year they're at 111.

They're holding teams to 43 percent shooting from the field, 3rd-best in the league and their lowest since 2011-12. Their 9.3 steals per game are 6th-most.

All five starters are among the top 25 players in the league in defensive rating – James is fourth, Embiid 11th, Edgecombe 15th, Maxey 22nd and Brown 23rd. How is that even possible?

It's rare to see superstar-caliber guys play as hard on the defensive end as the offensive end. Everybody on this team embraces it. They hustle, they work, they communicate and most importantly they commit to it.

The biggest concern when the 76ers built this dream team was that it would be a team of individuals out for themselves, but the reality has been the opposite.

In a very short period of time, they've learned how to play together. How to play for each other.

And we haven't even mentioned V.J. Edgecomb, who at 21 years old has figured out how to assimilate into this loaded lineup, never force anything, wait for his opportunities and make huge shots when he gets his turn. Edgecombe is at 12.7 points and 3.0 assists per game, and his numbers are understandably down a bit from last year, but if that bothers him it sure doesn't show.

And the role players – Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jabari Walker – have each adopted the same ego-free style of basketball, supporting the starters however they need to.

Nick Nurse deserves a ton of credit for getting this bunch to play this brand of hoops. It's not easy to get any NBA player to put team goals ahead of individual goals. But he's got Hall of Famers and all-stars doing it and having a blast along the way. They all seem to love playing basketball the right way and they seem to love playing together.

The 76ers are 7-1 and looking like a real threat to win the East, and they're doing it by playing the game the right way.

By committing to each other and not themselves.

#2770. UPDATED: Chicago Bears 16-Man Practice Squad

The Chicago Bears have a 16-man practice squad, but the list will be fluid, and we'll update it throughout the year.

UPDATE (11/4): The Bears signed TE Stephen Carlson to the active roster and signed DE Earnest Brown IV to the practice squad.

Practice squad injured: Anthony Johnson Jr. (S)

Here are the qualifications for practice squad eligibility and some rules to remember.

A 17th player is permitted as long as he qualifies for the NFL's International Pathway Program.

Players with no accrued seasons (rookies) and those with fewer than nine regular-season games in their lone accrued season.

A maximum of ten players are allowed who have earned no more than two accrued seasons.

Up to six players with unlimited accrued seasons are permitted on the practice squad.

However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players.

Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After the game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad. A player can be elevated up to three times, but if he's needed after that, the team would be required to sign him to the 53-man active roster.

Players on practice squads are free agents who can be signed to another team's active roster. A player's current club can't block him from leaving; they can only make a counteroffer to keep him. Ultimately, it's the player's decision. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for three weeks, but if he's released, he'll revert to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks' salary.

A practice squad player can't sign with his team's upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week.

#2769. INTERVIEW: Bayern sales chief Kasper on maintaining Kane hype and pushing other clubs to grow Bundesliga appeal

MÜNCHEN (Bulinews): Bayern Munich's social media pages boomed after Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or, but now the aim is to retain that level of interest. Tasked with fulfilling that role is the club's Marketing and Sales Officer, Rouven Kasper.

“It's difficult, you always have to look at what’s next. We have had strong momentum and are growing based on our media and commercial departments' clear strategy," Kasper told Bulinews.com at a media round in München.

“We have some disadvantages when it comes to international business, but we just need to work as a team with the Bundesliga and the other clubs. For sure, we have it in our hands to make it as good as possible.

“From recent years, it [development] has been very good. We can see now that we can make strong effects in the international field. This gives us even more power so we can invest into different platforms and new products.

“Maybe we can even open infrastructure in other continents, because when you have an office and people there you can learn more about the [local] market. Then you can adapt better. This is our next step," he pointed out.

The Bayern chief was also quick to demand greater output from Bundesliga clubs outside of Bayern and Borussia Dortmund. Kasper senses the other 16 teams in the topflight could play an important role in growing the league's appeal.

“The league needs to be better and bring more reach. We [Bayern Munich] are the spearhead of German football. Together with other the other clubs and the league, we need to be more active in the market.

“When you compare the last two years, there were 13 Premier League clubs playing abroad outside the UK [in pre-season] while Bundesliga clubs had five. At the end, it’s about people and being a community.

“We want to be approachable. We want to talk to the people and be there as the Bundesliga. Bayern along with Dortmund can’t do that alone, so we need more activity from the other clubs in different markets.

“The UK teams, also the Spanish [La Liga] are doing. We are doing our part, not only in the summer but also the winter. It requires team spirit and I think it needs to be pushed a little bit more,” said Kasper, claiming a need for cooperation.

#2768. Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double

Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season.

Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.

On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards.

The Sixers' absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team's matchup with the Pistons on Sunday.

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory Saturday:

Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James' place. He'd missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

The 3-and-D forward scored the night's first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession.

Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team's offense in the early going.

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man.

Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead.

One of Embiid's assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter.

The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn't enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter.

Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run.

Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn't carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly.

Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins' three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead.

The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they'd fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win.

The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team's transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game's first 19 fast-break points.

The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup.

Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup.

Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks' odds of a road win. They'd all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter.

Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers' lead to 97-87.

The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel'el Ware's put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee's deficit to 117-114.

The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure.

For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

#2767. “We deserved more” – Reaction to the City defeat

RB Leipzig battled hard against Manchester City on matchday 4 of the Champions League league phase but ultimately fell to a narrow 3-2 defeat. Here's what our boys had to say after the game.

On the game:"I think we deserved more than a point tonight. It was our best performance so far this season without the ball, and we showed plenty of attacking intent. We also played really well in possession overall. We only have ourselves to blame for the first goal we conceded. But I'm very pleased with the way we played and the performance of the whole team."

Looking ahead:"There are plenty of positives we can take from this game. Of course, it's disappointing not to get anything from it after a performance like that. But the players can be proud of how they played. We were up against an outstanding team, we learned a lot and now we have to keep going."

On the game:"We really wanted to win at home tonight and keep our good run going here. Against a team like City, it comes down to fine margins and key moments. We weren't quite at our best in those situations and didn't defend well enough. Even so, it was a good team performance and one we can build on."

On the team's development:"We tried to double up on their wide players because we knew how much individual quality they had. For large parts of the game, that worked well. But against teams like that, you have to keep it up for the full 90 minutes. Maybe that's the next step we still need to take as a team."

On his goal:"I'm obviously delighted with my goal. It's always nice when you can show what you can do on the pitch and get on the scoresheet. But for me, the team's performance matters more. I'd much rather have come away with the three points tonight."

On the game:"It's tough because I feel like we deserved more tonight. We've come away with no points, and that doesn't feel good. We should have made more of some of the good spells we had. I think we deserved at least a draw."

On City's clinical finishing:"We know how much quality they have. They don't need many chances to score. That's why you have to stay switched on for the full 90 minutes against a team like that. It's absolutely crucial."

On the game:"It's incredibly frustrating. I think we played really well for large parts of the game and gave everything we had. At home, you've got to come away with at least a point from a game like that. To end up with nothing tonight really hurts."

On his link-up play with Nusa:"We were always really dangerous when we broke forward. For large parts of the game, we did really well. But you have to manage games like that a bit more cleverly, so you at least come away with a point or give yourself the chance to win it right at the end."

On RBL's Champions League campaign so far:"We've got three points from four games now. That's not what we had in mind. We've faced some very tough opponents, but we've also shown that we can compete with them. Ultimately, though, that's not enough. You have to pick up points as well."

On the remaining Champions League fixtures:"I still believe in this team and that we can pick up more points in the Champions League. I think we'll need around ten points. We've got games coming up where we'll have the chance to get some points on the board, so now we've got to deliver."

#2766. Todd Monken: Deshaun Watson not ruled out yet, but Shedeur Sanders preparing to start

Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol after self-reporting symptoms on Tuesday.

Head coach Todd Monken told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that Watson hasn’t necessarily been ruled out for Sunday’s game against New Orleans. But the club is preparing Shedeur Sanders to start.

“What I would say is, credit to Deshaun — after the game, [he] felt fine. Monday night, started feeling a little bit, little bit of a headache, and came in Tuesday and, you know, reported,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “So, credit to him for someone who really loves playing the game. And so, he is in the protocol. And Shedeur will take the reps today with the ones.”

Monken admitted that it’s “a little more difficult” for a quarterback to play on Sunday after missing practice due to a concussion. But Monken and the team will let the process play out.

“I mean, there’s a long time between now and then, right? I mean, look where the Ravens are at. And you don’t know as the week goes on what could happen,” Monken said. “It’s not ideal, right? It’s not ideal for any player to go through a week and not practice and then play. We know that. But every situation is different.”

Monken noted that Watson can participate in the team’s meetings to help him stay prepared in the event that he gets cleared. The team has been game-planning with the idea that Sanders will start. But Monken said the game plan won’t change much if it’s Sanders or Watson behind center.

“I don’t see the way [it would change], because the rest of the guys are the same, and they’re similar in some ways,” Monken said. “Some things, you know, Shedeur’s skill set is different than Deshaun’s, but still very similar in terms of what we do. We can’t change that dramatically.”

Either way, Watson is expected to still be the starter when he is cleared.

“Yeah, I didn’t assume I’d get that question. Yeah, he’s been our starter for eight games. I would assume he’s still our starter,” Monken said. “I don’t — I’m thinking about Wednesday. But I’m not — I’m really thinking about today and watching Shedeur play today.”

So far this season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards with seven touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s been sacked a league-high 33 times. His eight games this season are the most he’s played in a year for the Browns since arriving on the club in 2022.

Last season, Sanders completed 56.6 percent of his throws for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games with seven starts.

#2764. Kyle Shanahan: Nothing's changed for me with Brandon Aiyuk, I've moved on mentally

When 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked in September if the team’s injury issues at wide receiver had led him to consider bringing Brandon Aiyuk back, his answer was a strong no.

Aiyuk has started the process of being reinstated from the team’s reserve/left squad list and part of that process would involve him reporting to the team’s facility later this week if he has not been released ahead of time. Shanahan was asked at a Wednesday press conference about any expectations he has about such a visit.

“None. I have no expectation,” Shanahan said. “I’ve kind of moved on with that mentally and doing kind of how I talked to you guys two months ago. Nothing’s really changed for me.”

Shanahan said he has not had any conversations about a roster exemption that would give the 49ers more time to explore a trade, which joins releasing him or welcoming him back to the active roster as the team’s options once he is off the left squad list. Shanahan said there are “no absolutes” when asked if he could envision any scenario where Aiyuk plays for the team again, but his other answers sent a strong message that Aiyuk will be moving on once the administrative work is done.

#2763. LeBron Log No. 3: The King dishes, Caitlin Clark visits and closing time

LeBron Log No. 3: The King dishes, Caitlin Clark visits and closing time originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James' latest week with the Sixers included his first 10-assist game with Philadelphia, his best performance with the team, a visit with Caitlin Clark, a crowd-wide finger wag and one jumper he would probably like back.

Some of it belonged in the box score. The rest quickly made its way around social media.

Welcome to the third edition of the LeBron Log.

Throughout the preseason, the Sixers discussed the responsibility that accompanied their desire to play faster.

They wanted to advance the ball before defenses could organize, but Nick Nurse was not interested in accepting extra turnovers as part of the tradeoff. When asked whether he could live with more mistakes if they came with better pace, his answer was simple.

Seven games into the regular season, the Sixers have not yet become one of the NBA's fastest teams. They entered Monday ranked 20th in pace.

Philadelphia has committed an NBA-low 12.7 turnovers per game. James has helped organize the offense as its leading facilitator, recording 35 assists against 11 turnovers.

He leads the Sixers in total assists despite playing only five games. Tyrese Maxey, who has appeared in all seven, is second with 31.

James provided the cleanest example Wednesday night against the Pacers. He finished with 13 points, 10 assists, five rebounds, two blocks and no turnovers during the Sixers' 114-109 comeback victory.

It was his first double-digit-assist performance with Philadelphia. According to StatMuse, James also became the oldest player in its database to record at least 10 points and 10 assists while committing no more than one turnover.

James' night was not flashy by his standards. He attempted 12 shots and finished fifth on the team in scoring. Still, he helped five Sixers reach double figures without surrendering a possession.

The Sixers signed the NBA's all-time leading scorer. Through the opening weeks of his Philadelphia career, he has been their leading passer.

James entered his first NBA Cup game with the Sixers possessing more tournament history than anyone else on the roster.

He led the Lakers to the inaugural Cup championship in 2023 and was named the event's first MVP after averaging 26.4 points, eight rebounds and seven assists during Los Angeles' unbeaten run.

Three years later, his first Cup game in red, white and blue produced his best Sixers performance yet.

James recorded 20 points, nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block in Friday's 98-93 win over the Knicks. He shot 8 for 15 and saved two of his most important baskets for the final 70 seconds.

Jalen Brunson's three-pointer gave New York a 90-89 lead with 1:32 remaining. On the ensuing possession, James backed down OG Anunoby, turned toward the middle and sank a fadeaway to move the Sixers back in front.

VJ Edgecombe extended the lead with a three-pointer as the shot clock expired. After Brunson made two free throws, Maxey drove for a layup and missed. James followed the play, collected the offensive rebound and scored the putback with 11.9 seconds remaining.

The basket sealed Philadelphia's second win over the defending champions and its first of NBA Cup group play.

"Best game all around," Nurse said. "He's been good, but that was his best game for sure."

James has played more than 1,600 regular-season games, but his Philadelphia closing reel has officially begun.

The fourth-quarter baskets were not James' only memorable moments Friday.

After converting an and-one earlier in the game, James broke out his familiar shoulder-shrug celebration. Edgecombe joined him, smiling as he mirrored the move alongside his 41-year-old teammate.

The pair had already developed a personalized handshake featuring two taps to the head and a forceful shrug. This one came during the game.

James supplied another recognizable celebration in the third quarter.

Anunoby drove toward the basket with James trailing the play. James caught him near the rim and was officially credited with his fifth block of the season.

He turned toward the crowd and wagged his finger. The fans joined in.

Edgecombe later delivered the biggest shot of the game, and James met him with an embrace near the sideline. The two are separated by more than 20 years, but they have quickly developed a collection of celebrations.

"He doesn't shy away from the moment," James said of the 21-year-old. "Young kid, but he thrives in the moment."

James was not the only basketball attraction inside Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Wednesday.

Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark watched the Sixers' win from courtside and brought a small camera with her. It was the second time this year she photographed James during a game.

In March, Clark served as a credentialed photographer when James and the Lakers visited Indiana.

"The KING 👑 … Shot by ME," Clark wrote when she shared those photos.

After Wednesday's game, Clark made her way toward the visiting locker room. She briefly met Maxey before speaking with James in the hallway.

James gave Clark one of his No. 23 Sixers jerseys. The team shared photos of the exchange with a fitting caption.

Clark publicly expressed hope that James would join the Pacers before he signed with Philadelphia. Their mutual respect goes back further.

During Clark's first WNBA season in 2024, James compared the attention surrounding her professional debut to what he experienced when he entered the NBA directly from high school.

"I'm rooting for Caitlin because I've been in that seat before," James said at the time. "I've walked that road before."

James did not speak with reporters after Wednesday's game, so he was not asked about their conversation.

Maxey was asked about meeting Clark for the first time.

"That's just another person that I like to watch," he said. "She cold. She nice. Seeing her today was really cool. Sometimes you try not to fan out, but it was really cool seeing her. It's her building; she plays here too."

James and Edgecombe also produced the week's most widely shared Sixers warmup clip.

Before Wednesday's game, the two danced together near the three-point line. Edgecombe moved away while James stepped back and launched a jumper.

The clip spread quickly across social media. James still walked out of downtown Indianapolis with 10 assists, no turnovers and a victory.

James has made more field goals than anyone in NBA history. Even the career scoring leader is entitled to one warmup mulligan.

#2762. NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 2026 Start ‘Em Sit ‘Em: Kicker

NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 2026 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Kicker appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

A strong fantasy football kicker doesn't always need to be part of one of the NFL's most productive offenses. For instance, Washington's Drew Stevens showcased this against Philadelphia, turning a game with limited touchdown opportunities into one of the best kicking performances of Week 8.

The challenge for fantasy managers is to identify which offenses can consistently reach scoring territory without solely relying on touchdowns. Analyzing recent field-goal volume can provide valuable insights, although factors such as the opponent and changing offensive circumstances can turn even yesterday's reliable starters into risky choices.

Week 9 offers several intriguing opportunities, including Chicago's improving offense and a Las Vegas kicker who has quietly become a significant fantasy contributor. Meanwhile, other familiar names are facing tough matchups or uncertainties regarding their roles. Here are the kickers to start and sit this week.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Cairo Santos has emerged as a promising streaming option as the Chicago Bears continue to find ways to score. In their recent game against Seattle, which they won 34-17 on Monday Night Football, Santos contributed two field goals and four extra points. His successful field goals were from distances of 38 and 44 yards, adding to a productive streak that included three field goals against New England in Week 7. The Bears have scored at least 30 points in three of their last four games, providing Santos with a much stronger offensive foundation than earlier this season. The team is creating scoring opportunities through various strategies, reducing their reliance on any single aspect of their offense.

Tampa Bay poses an intriguing matchup since its defense has shown the capability to disrupt opposing offenses. The Buccaneers recently shut out Atlanta, demonstrating their ability to keep opponents from reaching the end zone. This situation could favor Santos if Chicago maintains its recent offensive success while facing tougher resistance near the goal line.

Additionally, the Bears have displayed confidence in allowing Santos to attempt longer field goals, as he connected from 58 yards against New England, indicating that his scoring opportunities are not limited to shorter attempts.

Matt Gay has been one of the more productive kickers in fantasy football over the past eight weeks, despite playing for a Las Vegas team that has struggled to achieve consistent results. The Raiders scored 38 points against the Jets last weekend, and Gay contributed with a 53-yard field goal and five successful extra points. This performance continues a productive stretch in which Las Vegas has regularly provided him with scoring opportunities.

This season, Gay has converted 18 field goals, including several crucial attempts during close games. His performance against Kansas City in Week 4 was particularly impressive; he made all four attempts in a narrow 30-27 defeat. Although San Francisco is a tougher opponent, the matchup still holds significant fantasy value. The 49ers have faced challenges in preventing opposing teams from creating scoring opportunities, and the Raiders have shown they can move the ball against defenses with more established reputations.

Gay's value lies in the various ways he can contribute. The Raiders have generated enough touchdowns to create extra-point opportunities while also settling for field goals during crucial possessions. Given the potential for another competitive game, he is an appealing option, especially since his recent accuracy indicates he can capitalize when Las Vegas reaches scoring range.

Drew Stevens delivered an impressive performance against Philadelphia, converting four out of five field-goal attempts and adding an extra point during Washington's 27-10 victory. His successful attempts included a remarkable 56-yard field goal, showcasing the range that makes him especially valuable in fantasy leagues that award additional points for longer kicks.

While Washington's offense has struggled with consistency, Stevens has benefited whenever the Commanders advance into opposing territory without finishing drives with touchdowns. He has converted 14 of 17 field-goal attempts this season, including successful kicks from 55, 56, and 57 yards.

The upcoming matchup against the Rams is promising for a kicker capable of scoring from a distance. Los Angeles has allowed opposing kickers to accumulate significant fantasy points, and Washington may need to capitalize on every scoring opportunity to stay competitive.

Harrison Butker's fantasy value has become increasingly unpredictable, especially in light of Kansas City's recent offensive struggles. In Week 7 against Seattle, he converted only one of three field-goal attempts, and his performance did not improve against Denver, where he missed one of two attempts during the Chiefs' 28-24 loss. These inconsistencies raise concerns about his reliability at a time when fantasy managers need consistent production.

Together with that, Kansas City has brought in competition for the kicker position by signing veteran Justin Tucker to its practice squad in late October. While this does not necessarily mean Butker has lost his starting job, it introduces uncertainty to a situation that previously seemed stable.

The upcoming matchup against the Jets is also concerning. New York has been effective at limiting opportunities for opposing kickers to score high fantasy points, while Kansas City's offense has struggled to maintain consistent scoring in recent weeks.

Chad Ryland has achieved impressive field-goal totals this season; however, his upcoming matchup raises significant concerns. In Week 6, the Cardinals' kicker successfully converted all six of his attempts against the Rams, delivering an exceptional fantasy performance in a game where Arizona struggled to finish drives with touchdowns. He followed that performance with three successful field goals against Denver and two more against Dallas, solidifying his valuable role in Arizona's offense.

Unfortunately, the upcoming game against Seattle poses challenges. Earlier this season, the Seahawks defeated the Cardinals 31-7, preventing Arizona from even attempting a single field goal.

Although Ryland's accuracy and range are encouraging, the risk of another game with limited scoring opportunities makes him a potentially risky fantasy starter. Fantasy managers should consider prioritizing kickers on teams with more reliable scoring chances this week

Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images

Jake Elliott is facing a frustrating situation as the Philadelphia Eagles struggle to maintain offensive production. Last weekend, the Eagles scored only 10 points against Washington, and Elliott successfully converted just one of his two field-goal attempts. Throughout October, his opportunities have been limited. Philadelphia did not attempt a field goal against Carolina in Week 6 or Dallas in Week 7, leaving Elliott reliant solely on extra points. This inconsistent workload has made him difficult to trust, despite his proven kicking ability.

While the Giants may seem to present a favorable opportunity, the Eagles' recent struggles indicate that fantasy managers should be cautious about anticipating a sudden increase in scoring chances. The team has consistently failed to convert offensive possessions into reliable scoring, meaning Elliott cannot generate fantasy points without opportunities.

He still has the potential to deliver a strong performance if Philadelphia's offense improves, but the recent lack of attempts makes him a risky choice when better streaming options are available.

Chicago's improved offensive production makes Santos a tempting fantasy option. Meanwhile, Gay and Stevens have shown they can score points with longer field goals.

However, Butker's recent accuracy issues, along with Arizona's tough matchup and Philadelphia's inconsistent offense, suggest that there are better choices available. For Week 9, managers should focus on available field-goal opportunities instead of assuming that a well-known kicker will automatically provide a reliable fantasy score.

#2758. Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1

Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers kept up their hot start to the season Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, reaching 7-1 with a 126-107 win against the Bulls.

All five of the Sixers' starters scored in double figures. Tyrese Maxey posted 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown tallied a season-best 25 points and 11 rebounds.

VJ Edgecombe's 21 points were a new season high. LeBron James recorded 15 points, nine assists and seven boards.

Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson had 24 points and seven rebounds.

Joel Embiid (15 points, eight rebounds) had been listed as questionable with an official designation of "right foot plantar fascia injury management." He sat out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back for the Sixers' win over the Hornets.

"Plantar is a little bit of a come and go type of thing," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters pregame. "They're just trying to manage it. It's very painful, if you've ever had it. It can kind of come and go out of nowhere. So we're just trying to manage the pain with that, be as smart as we can."

Nurse told reporters that Dominick Barlow is set to see a specialist Tuesday about the back injury that's sidelined him to start the season.

"He's been on court a little bit … not a ton of moving around," Nurse said. "I think they want to get to tomorrow's appointment. Hopefully, it'll be positive and we can get into his workouts a little bit."

The Sixers will begin a three-game road trip Wednesday when they visit the Pistons. Here are observations on their victory Monday:

After Embiid blitzed a Bulls pick-and-roll, Maxey picked off Matas Buzelis' hurried pass to get the Sixers rolling in transition and James jammed home the team's first field goal.

Edgecombe got a slam soon after James grabbed a defensive rebound and the Sixers again pushed the pace. The Sixers scored six quick fast-break points, leading the Bulls to burn an early timeout, and James' long-distance feeds were a major asset.

"If you're open, he's going to pass it," Edgecombe said of James. "The main thing is just being ready. Tonight I had to run and go get 'em. If you're open and he sees you, he's going to pass the ball."

Edgecombe had a dunk-heavy first quarter. He threw down his second when Dean Wade nabbed a steal and dropped off a typically selfless dish to the Sixers' explosive second-year guard, whose slam put the team up 22-13.

The Sixers have an abundance of dangerous options in the open floor, Edgecombe included. As he's already shown with his continued clutch shotmaking, the 21-year-old won't become anything resembling a non-factor offensively this year as a byproduct of the Sixers' enhanced star power.

Over the team's first seven games, Edgecombe had averaged 11.3 points. He scored 11 in the first period on 5-for-5 shooting.

Adem Bona missed a dunk early in the second quarter, which stung a bit more when Jalen Smith drilled a three-pointer seconds later.

Bona remained the Sixers' main backup center. He had a poor first-half stint overall amid a largely negative start to his third season. The 23-year-old big man played well in the Sixers' victory over the Bucks, posting six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Outside of that, his season has been sparse on bright moments so far. It's reasonable to wonder when Nurse might turn to alternatives like Jabari Walker, who played a good game Saturday in Charlotte, or try James again at the five.

The Bulls outscored the Sixers by eight points in Bona's first run, cutting their derficit to 40-38. Chicago went in front with a three by former Sixer Buddy Hield.

The Sixers regained the advantage late in the second quarter. Maxey and James each were excellent as passers in the first half, combining for 14 assists and three turnovers. James fired the ball to Wade for a corner three that gave the Sixers a 60-52 lead.

Following a third-quarter Embiid fadeaway jumper and two James lay-ins, the Sixers were up 17 points.

The Bulls cut the Sixers' lead down to 11 points by the start of the fourth quarter. With Bona still struggling and on four fouls, Wade began the fourth at center. Bona then briefly spelled Wade before being whistled for his fifth foul and taking a seat. Embiid ultimately wasn't needed for any of the fourth period and only logged 25 minutes.

Embiid said postgame that he was not available to return to the action in the fourth and has been feeling his plantar fasciitis on the court. The seven-time All-Star's health is clearly not close to 100 percent.

"I was on a minutes restriction," he said. "(The foot) has been going like that for the past few weeks. It's painful. Just got to manage it.

"If it flares up pretty bad, got to take a step back. We've been able to manage it, but it has its ups and downs."

The Sixers' lead got as low as eight points, but Chicago did not shoot well enough from three-point range (26.3 percent) or have sufficient firepower to sustain a meaningful comeback run. The bottom line is the Sixers are in a different class than the Bulls, who fell to 1-6.

As for the Sixers, they'll wake up Tuesday morning at the top of the Eastern Conference standings.

"You've got some of these nights where you kind of call them professional wins. …You look at the records and all that kind of stuff, but they have a lot of talent," Nurse said. "A lot of these teams play a way that's a little scary. It's fast and it's furious, lots of threes. … They're going to keep coming at you, high-possession games. So they're not easy games and I'm glad that we handled it professionally tonight."

#2756. Derrick Barnes Reveals Emotional Lions Locker Room Moment After Jack Campbell Injury

The Detroit Lions are preparing for another football game, but Derrick Barnes made one thing perfectly clear Wednesday: Their injured teammate, Jack Campbell, remains at the center of everything they're doing.

And what happened after Sunday's emotional victory over the Minnesota Vikings reveals just how deeply Campbell's injury has affected the organization.

Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez, Joe Bachie, and other members of Detroit's linebacker group made their way to the hospital following the game, hoping to support the teammate they had just watched suffer a frightening neck injury.

But for Barnes, the experience demonstrated something about the relationships inside Detroit's locker room that no football game could ever fully explain.

Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) catches a pass in front of Detroit Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes (55) during the fourth quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

For most NFL players, a dramatic divisional victory would provide plenty of reasons to celebrate. That wasn't what Barnes was thinking about after Detroit defeated Minnesota 19-15.

During an emotional conversation with reporters Wednesday, Barnes described the anxiety he experienced while trying to reach the hospital after the game.

"I'm weaving through traffic — kids, don't do that at home — but, no, man, I haven't felt this way in a long time," Barnes said. "Just heart beating real fast, anxious, nervous, kind of scared a little bit."

Although Barnes and his fellow linebackers couldn't visit Campbell directly, simply gathering at the hospital provided an opportunity to lean on one another.

For a group that spends nearly every day working together, watching one of their brothers suffer such a frightening injury had been overwhelming.

Barnes also explained why being there mattered so much to him.

"I always thought, 'Jack would do the same thing for me. He would do the same thing for everybody in this locker room.'"

Those words say plenty about the type of teammate Campbell has become.

Barnes wasn't alone in struggling emotionally.

Malcolm Rodriguez described watching Campbell remain on the field after the injury, desperately hoping his teammate would get back to his feet.

Rodriguez acknowledged that he eventually began thinking about Campbell's family and what they must have been experiencing.

The emotions became too much to hold back.

"You're in the game, you're trying to lock back in, but you're still — he's on your mind," Rodriguez said.

Barnes admitted that he also cried, explaining that he couldn't remember the last time a situation had affected him so deeply.

That's an important reminder of what NFL players experience during moments like Sunday's injury.

Fans see the game, the replays, and the final score. The players see a close friend whose health and future suddenly become far more important than the outcome.

As we reported following Barnes' emotional comments immediately after Sunday's victory, the Lions found motivation to finish the game for Campbell.

But that determination didn't make the concern disappear when the clock reached zero.

Wednesday also brought news that provided a much-needed emotional lift.

In a statement released through the Detroit Lions, Campbell revealed that he has full movement in his lower body and continues making progress with movement in his upper body.

The update followed several difficult days for Campbell, his family, and everyone associated with the organization.

Barnes admitted that hearing the news gave him an immediate boost.

As we previously covered following Campbell's personal statement, the linebacker remains optimistic while acknowledging that his recovery will require continued work.

There is still no announced timetable for Campbell's return to football.

For his teammates, however, knowing he is making progress is far more important than when he might be able to play again.

Detroit's next challenge arrives Sunday against the Miami Dolphins.

Barnes could be asked to take over some of Campbell's defensive communication duties, including potentially wearing the green-dot helmet used to relay calls from the sideline.

Campbell has become the central communicator of Detroit's defense, and his absence creates challenges that extend beyond tackles, coverage assignments, and individual production.

But Barnes isn't approaching the opportunity as an attempt to replace his teammate.

Instead, he's drawing inspiration from the standard Campbell has established.

Barnes explained that defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has encouraged the defense to carry that mentality forward.

"That's kind of my mentality: just pick up wherever he left off. That's inspired a lot of us. Basically, from now, it's for him."

Barnes also admitted that the injury caused him to reflect on the risks that come with playing football, even making a half-serious comment to his young son about potentially avoiding the sport.

It was a rare moment of vulnerability from someone whose job demands extraordinary physical and mental toughness.

Detroit has dealt with adversity before, but this situation is different.

The Lions aren't simply trying to overcome the absence of an All-Pro linebacker. They're supporting a teammate whose recovery matters far more than wins, losses, or playoff positioning.

He also understands why Campbell would want his teammates to continue preparing, competing, and giving everything they have.

That doesn't mean forgetting what happened Sunday.

It means carrying their teammate's example into every practice, every meeting, and every game while continuing to support him and his family.

For Barnes, Rodriguez, and the rest of Detroit's defense, the motivation has become deeply personal.

And as the Lions prepare to take the field in Miami, those six words explain what will be driving them.

#2753. ‘I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers

'I'm finding my footing': Jaylen Brown's role taking shape with Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Jaylen Brown has spent the opening weeks of the season describing the Sixers as a work in progress.

He offered a similarly humble perspective Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena. His performance, however, provided the clearest look yet at how he can influence this group while sharing the floor with the club's other established stars.

Brown finished with 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists in the Sixers' 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls. He shot 9 for 15 from the field, made four three-pointers and did not commit a turnover.

Five of his rebounds came on the offensive end, an area Brown has emphasized while the Sixers continue piecing together their frontcourt rotation.

"Just a mindset," Brown said. "Just trying to create extra opportunities for my team. As we're trying to patch together our fives and our front line, I try to make an extra contribution and emphasis on the glass."

Brown has also been careful about how he describes his place on a roster that already belonged to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey.

Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter Monday, continuing his torrid start to the season. He has led the Sixers in scoring while being the only starter to appear in all eight games.

Brown is not interested in interrupting that.

"Maxey's been leading the way, 100 percent," Brown said. "He's been here. This is his team. Him and Joel have been here for a while, so the mindset has been to complement those guys. I'm finding my footing, but Maxey has been leading the way for sure."

Brown's footing looked firm against Chicago.

Beyond his scoring, he helped the Sixers control the glass, moved the ball within an offense that generated 23 assists during the first half and supplied the physicality Nick Nurse expects from him.

"The dude is tough and he wins," Nurse said. "I'll take that all day long. The degree of difficulty on some of the shots he hit was really amazing. I thought he pounded the glass and got some key rebounds. Makes a lot of winning plays. Man, he's a winner."

Brown spent the first 10 years of his career in Boston. He won a championship there, reached another NBA Finals and grew from a 20-year-old prospect into one of the league's premier two-way wings.

Moving into a new system alongside James, Embiid and Maxey was never going to be seamless.

"I mean, he's fitting in along with all of us," James said. "We're getting better and better. It's not going to happen overnight. He spent his first 10 years in a system in Boston, in the city, so it's going to take some adjustment.

"It takes adjustment for him. It's going to take adjustment for the rest of the guys that joined this franchise as well. But tonight was a great step."

James pointed to Brown's "pressure, his shot-making ability, his rebounding ability" and his professionalism.

Brown's early influence has extended beyond his production.

The Sixers entered Monday with one of the NBA's best half-court defenses. Brown has been one of the group's most persistent voices, stressing communication, preparation and attention to opposing players' tendencies.

"That's the part that I care about the most as a group, not individually," Brown said. "Having a mentality night in and night out, respecting your opponent, respecting the game, making sure that we are executing our coverages, we're being clear in our communication and then we're also taking away tendencies on a night-to-night basis.

"Those things I just explained are over 50 percent of the battle."

Brown understands that maintaining those details across an 82-game schedule will require more than reminders.

"A little bit of accountability," he said. "You learn different guys require different things. How you communicate with each guy may be a little different, but accountability for sure and confrontation if need be.

"The offense is going to be what it's going to be, but our defense has got to be non-negotiable. That's something I say all the time. Non-negotiable. You want to be a good team, defense is non-negotiable."

The Sixers showed both sides of their defensive potential Monday.

They built a double-digit lead during the first half, allowed Chicago to score 36 points in the second quarter and then created separation after halftime. Philadelphia held the Bulls to 20 points in the third quarter before pulling away in the fourth.

Brown did not celebrate their ability to raise their intensity after it slipped.

"I don't like that we have that," he said. "It's good that we have shown the potential, but we've got to keep that switch on. It doesn't work like that where you just flip the switch.

"It can catch up to us and it can bite us against a better team or on a night that we're not being as crisp on offense. It can't be a switch just because we're playing a lesser opponent or whatever the case may be. We've got to make sure that mentality is from the beginning to end. Can't skip any steps."

That urgency accompanies considerable optimism.

Brown said the Sixers enjoy playing together. He loves when James grabs a rebound because "he's like a quarterback," capable of launching an outlet pass or immediately pushing the pace.

The group is learning when to attack, when to move the ball and how to avoid hesitating in its effort to play unselfishly.

"It's a lot of talent, man," Brown said. "We like each other, and we're just kind of building that chemistry of how we can get this thing to a well-oiled machine. I think we're taking steps forward every single day."

The Sixers are 7-1 despite Brown believing those steps remain incomplete. They have won close games, erased sizable deficits and received important contributions from different players.

Brown's performance Monday showed another version of how their pieces can fit.

"We still have a long way to go to being a really, really solid, great team," Brown said. "But we've been able to win some games. We started out the season great, 7-1, and you haven't seen our best version yet.

#2748. LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it

LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James is one of kind in so many ways. What he did Monday night might be the cherry on top.

In the third quarter of the Sixers' 126-107 victory over the Bulls, James decided he'd take fan interaction to a whole new level.

James looked for a transition pass from Tyrese Maxey, who snagged a rebound. James was behind the pass and his momentum took him into the stands, where he disappeared for a few moments.

It wasn't until another angle was shown on replay that we could see what actually went down in the darkness of the seats. James didn't hold back giving reporters a play-by-play.

"I spilled some of his wine," he said postgame. "I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright."

Troy Clemons – the Sixers fan whose drink spilled – explained his perspective on the interaction with James to Kris Rhim of ESPN.

"[I was] walking to my seat … LeBron crashed into me, he grabbed me, he said 'My bad,' my drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the [court]."

"At the end of the day he's another man like me," Clemons said. "I mean he's LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it's nothing up with him, I just got a fresh drink though."

It should be noted that players are not supposed to drink from fans' cups, but it's rare for the NBA to fine someone for a spontaneous interaction such as this. In 2019, a similar thing happened when Mike Scott tumbled into the Bucks' court-side seats. The Sixers star jokingly took a sip of a fan's beverage and the NBA opted not to fine him. Time will tell if James has the same fate.

If nothing else, an interaction like this just shows how much fun James seems to be having.

The 24-year veteran noted the importance of finding joy in the game as he grinds through the season.

"It's a long marathon. And if you don't find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you're working and even though you're locked in, then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments, these fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well. By playing the game the right way, playing the game hard and then also just being showmen as well, it was a great game for us."

Head coach Nick Nurse also weighed in on the 41-year-old's mindset coming into the season.

"This summer I think he probably stated publicly that he wanted to go some place and have some fun playing. He loves the game, [it's his] 24th year. It's a group of guys, like I keep saying, that have been super focused in the intent of playing the right way. I think he's a big part of that."

The vibes are high. It's difficult for them not to be.

With Monday's win against the Bulls, the Sixers are 7-1 and lead the Eastern Conference. They've won four in a row and the only team they've lost to is the Pistons. The Sixers will face them on Wednesday to start a three-game road trip.

#2738. Now 26 years old, Tyrese Maxey’s career trajectory remains remarkable

Happy Birthday to Tyrese Maxey, who turns 26 years old today.

Between the Jaylen Brown trade and LeBron James signing for a minimum deal this offseason, it became easy to overlook just how important Maxey is to the Philadelphia 76ers franchise. The first eight games of the regular season have fixed that issue, with Tyrese exploding for 29.1 points per game on 50.3 percent shooting from the field, while also averaging 4.1 rebounds, 5.3 assists, 1.8 steals and 0.9 blocks. Maxey is even shooting well below career numbers from behind the arc over this small sample, so we could very well be looking at him averaging over 30 points per game this season. With the Sixers currently sitting with a 7-1 record, Tyrese is rightfully getting some early MVP conversation buzz. As Jaylen Brown said yesterday, this is Maxey's team.

We often neglect to account for how improbable Maxey reaching this point truly is within the bigger picture. He slipped to 21st overall in the 2020 NBA draft; players taken outside the lottery rarely reach All-NBA levels. Shooting was regarded as a weakness in his game and Tyrese has worked to become one of the absolute best shooters in the world. Maxey is a 6-foot-2 guard who was viewed as a defensive liability, and has now progressed to being a genuinely positively impactful player on that end of the court. The one percent better every day mantra could just be cute slogan for 99.9 percent of the population; for Maxey, he actually goes out and achieves it.

Maxey is already the career three-point field goals leader in Sixer franchise history (936 and counting). He currently sits 12th in franchise history on the scoring list, and barring injury, he'll be at least 10th at the end of the season. At his current trajectory, it would only take about six more seasons of similar play following this one for Tyrese to become the franchise's all-time leading scorer. We could very well be in the middle of watching the most prolific Sixers career ever.

Looking back, it's fair to argue Maxey saved this franchise from bottoming out for at least the next half decade. Without him around, the locker room may very well have imploded during the rough patch of recent years. Maybe the front office decides to do the full reset and strip things down to the studs. Mike Gansey likely doesn't think it's worth giving up future draft capital to acquire Jaylen Brown. LeBron James certainly doesn't sign here without Maxey's presence. It's a dark sliding doors world where Mike Muscala doesn't hit that shot and Tyrese Maxey doesn't end up a Sixer. Happy Birthday, Tyrese! We are very, very glad to have you.

#2733. Major Setback For LIV 2.0 As BC Partners Pulls Out Of Financing Deal

BC Partners, the investment firm that stepped in to replace the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) as financiers for LIV Golf, have pulled out of their deal with LIV Golf League. BC Partners had originally committed to investing $300 million in LIV Golf League, providing much needed funding for LIV Golf 2.0, the supposed next chapter of LIV Golf League. The move by BC Partners will be a major setback for the continued survival of LIV Golf.

Only a handful of players had publicly committed to playing LIV Golf 2.0. Those players were Richard Bland, Cameron Tringale, Brendan Steele, and Ben Campbell. Many of LIV Golf's stars have since departed the league, including Tyrrell Hatton, Jon Rahm, and Sergio Garcia, with still others having departed even earlier. Those players include Brooks Koepka, Patrick Reed, and Eugenio Chacarra. Still, others remain in limbo, including Dustin Johnson and others who are hoping to negotiate with the Saudi PIF regarding unpaid contracts.

Koepka rejoined the PGA Tour in 2026 under the PGA Tour's returning member program, which included program eligibility requirements such as having won certain tournaments within 2022-2025 as well as a short application window. Many other LIV golfers did not take that route. It's presumed that those ex-LIV golfers with status on the DP World Tour will play on that tour for the 2027 season.

LIV Golf had previously filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on September 8, 2026 in order to restructure the league's debts and obligations. The bankruptcy proceedings were originally intended to give LIV Golf time to address prior financial obligations and to complete it's transaction with BC Partners.

A hearing is scheduled in US Bankruptcy Court for LIV Golf on November 5. However, it's likely that without financing from BC Partners, LIV Golf will be headed towards a liquidation of its assets.
